title.zh: 卷一百六十七 列傳第九十二 白裴崔韋二李皇甫王
title.en: Volume 167 Biographies 92: Bai, Pei, Cui, Wei, two Li's, Huang, Fu, Wang
title.raw: 卷一百六十七 列傳第九十二 白裴崔韋二李皇甫王 Volume 167 Biographies 92: Bai, Pei, Cui, Wei, two Li's, Huang, Fu, Wang

sentences.zh: 白裴崔韋二李皇甫王

translations.literal: Bai, Pei, Cui, Wei, two Li's, Huangfu, Wang
translations.idiomatic: Bai, Pei, Cui, Wei, the two Lis, Huangfu, and Wang

sentences.zh: 白志貞者，本名琇珪，故太原史也。

translations.literal: Bai Zhizhen—his original name was Xiugui—was formerly a clerk in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zhizhen, whose original name was Xiugui, had once served as a clerk in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 事節度使李光弼，硁硁自力，有智數。

translations.literal: He served the military governor Li Guangbi, was steadfast and self-reliant, and possessed resourcefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Under the military governor Li Guangbi he proved diligent and self-reliant, and showed a shrewd mind for strategy.

sentences.zh: 光弼善之，使與帳下議。

translations.literal: Guangbi favored him and had him take part in council with his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi took a liking to him and brought him into deliberations with his staff.

sentences.zh: 代宗素聞，及光弼卒，擢累司農卿。

translations.literal: Suzong had long heard of him; when Guangbi died, he was promoted in succession to Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong had already heard of his reputation, and after Guangbi's death he was promoted step by step until he reached the post of Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 在官十年，德宗以為敏，遂倚腹心，進授神策軍使，賜今名。

translations.literal: After ten years in office, Dezong regarded him as quick-witted and relied on him as a trusted confidant, advancing him to command the Shence Army and bestowing his present name.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for ten years; Emperor Dezong found him sharp-witted, made him a trusted confidant, appointed him commander of the Shence Army, and granted him the name he now bore.

sentences.zh: 有所建白，善窺億帝指，故言無不從。

translations.literal: Whenever he offered proposals he was skilled at divining the emperor's intent, so none of his words went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: In whatever he proposed he had a knack for reading the emperor's mind, so that the throne never refused his advice.

sentences.zh: 從狩奉天，以為行在都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: He followed the hunt to Fengtian and was made overall commander of troops at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew to Fengtian on campaign, he was named overall commander of troops at the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 懼李懷光暴其惡，乃與趙贊、盧杞等抑懷光不使朝。

translations.literal: Fearing that Li Huaiguang would expose his crimes, he joined Zhao Zan, Lu Qi, and others in restraining Huaiguang from attending court.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid Li Huaiguang would expose his misdeeds, he worked with Zhao Zan, Lu Qi, and others to keep Huaiguang from coming to court.

sentences.zh: 懷光反，論斥其奸，貶恩州司馬，贊播州司馬。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang rebelled, their treachery was denounced in debate; Bai was demoted to prefectural aide in Enzhou, Zan to the same rank in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiguang rose in rebellion, their scheming was publicly condemned; Bai was demoted to prefectural aide in En Prefecture and Zan to the same office in Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 稍徙閬州別駕。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to be vice-prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later moved to the post of vice-prefect of Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，起為果州刺史，宰相李勉固諫，不許。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was recalled to serve as prefect of Guozhou; the chief minister Li Mian remonstrated firmly, but the emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: In 786 he was recalled as prefect of Guo Prefecture; Chief Minister Li Mian protested strongly, yet the emperor would not be dissuaded.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜浙西觀察使，死於官。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed military commissioner of Zhexi and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed military commissioner of Western Zhe and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡，河中河東人。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling was a native of Hezhong in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling came from Hezhong in the Hedong region.

sentences.zh: 乾元末，為汜水尉，賊陷東都，去客江夏。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianyuan era he was magistrate of Qishui; when rebels seized the Eastern Capital he left and lodged as a guest in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Qianyuan reign he served as magistrate of Qishui; when rebels took the Eastern Capital he fled and stayed as a guest in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 華州刺史董晉表署判官，稍遷太常博士。

translations.literal: The Huazhou prefect Dong Jin recommended him as a judicial aide, and he was gradually promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jin, prefect of Hua Prefecture, had him appointed judicial aide, and he rose in time to the post of Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 盧杞秉政，引為膳部員外郎、集賢院直學士。

translations.literal: When Lu Qi held power he was brought in as an outer-office member of the Board of Provisions and a resident academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qi dominated the government, he was brought in as an outer-office member of the Board of Provisions and a resident academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 崔造表知東都度支院。

translations.literal: Cui Zao memorialized that he should oversee the Eastern Capital revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao recommended him to oversee the Eastern Capital revenue office.

sentences.zh: 召為祠部郎中，不待命，輒還集賢院，宰相張延賞疾其易，出為昭應令。

translations.literal: He was summoned as director of the Board of Sacrifices, but without awaiting orders he went straight back to the Hall of Assembled Worthies; the chief minister Zhang Yanshang, resenting his presumption, had him sent out as magistrate of Zhaoying.
translations.idiomatic: He was called up as director of the Board of Sacrifices, yet without waiting for formal orders he returned at once to the Hall of Assembled Worthies; Chief Minister Zhang Yanshang, offended by his insolence, had him posted out as magistrate of Zhaoying.

sentences.zh: 與尉交訴所賕，京兆尹鄭叔則佑尉，而御史中丞竇參善延齡，卒逐尹。

translations.literal: He and the district magistrate sued each other over bribes; the Jingzhao intendant Zheng Shuzhe favored the magistrate, but the censor-in-chief Dou Can favored Yanling, and in the end the intendant was driven out.
translations.idiomatic: He and the district magistrate brought mutual suits over bribery; Jingzhao Intendant Zheng Shuzhe sided with the magistrate, but Censor-in-Chief Dou Can favored Yanling, and in the end the intendant was forced from office.

sentences.zh: 德宗用參輔政，即擢延齡司農少卿。

translations.literal: When Dezong employed Can to assist in government, Yanling was at once promoted to vice-minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dezong put Dou Can in charge of policy, Yanling was promptly promoted to vice-minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 會班宏卒，假領度支。

translations.literal: When Ban Hong died, he was given acting charge of the revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Ban Hong died, he was given acting charge of the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 延齡素不善財計，乃廣鉤距，取宿奸老吏與謀，以固帝幸。

translations.literal: Yanling had never been skilled at accounts; he therefore cast a wide net of schemes, took seasoned corrupt old clerks into counsel, and sought to secure the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling had never been adept at finance; he cast about for schemes instead, enlisted veteran corrupt clerks in his plots, and worked to secure the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 因建言：「左藏，天下歲入不資，耗登不可校。

translations.literal: He therefore proposed: "The left treasury—the empire's annual intake cannot support it, and waste and receipts cannot be checked.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed: "The left treasury cannot cover the empire's annual intake, and waste and receipts are beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 請列別舍，以檢盈虛。」

translations.literal: Please set up separate storehouses to inspect surplus and deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Let separate storehouses be established to audit surplus and shortfall.

sentences.zh: 於是以天下宿負八百萬緡析為負庫，抽貫三百萬緡為賸庫，樣物三十萬緡為季庫，帛以素出、以色入者為月庫。

translations.literal: Thereupon the empire's long-standing debts of eight million strings were split into a debt storehouse, drawn advances of three million into a surplus storehouse, sample goods of three hundred thousand into a quarterly storehouse, and silk issued in plain weave but received in colored weave into a monthly storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly the empire's long-standing debts of eight million strings were carved into a "debt vault," drawn advances of three million into a "surplus vault," sample goods worth three hundred thousand into a "quarterly vault," and silk issued in plain weave but received in dyed weave into a "monthly vault."

sentences.zh: 帝皆可之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 然天下負皆窮人，償入無期，抽貫與給皆盡；

translations.literal: Yet all the empire's debts were owed by the destitute, with no date for repayment; drawn advances and disbursements were already exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Yet every debt on the books belonged to the destitute, with no prospect of repayment; drawn advances and disbursements were already exhausted;

sentences.zh: 樣物與帛固有籍，延齡但多其薄最吏員以詭帝，於財用無所加也。

translations.literal: sample goods and silk already had their registers—Yanling merely inflated the ledgers and clerks to deceive the emperor, adding nothing to actual revenue.
translations.idiomatic: sample goods and silk already had their registers—Yanling merely inflated the ledgers and staff rolls to deceive the emperor, adding nothing to the treasury's real resources.

sentences.zh: 俄以戶部侍郎為真。

translations.literal: Before long he received the substantive post of vice-minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received the substantive post of vice-minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 又請以京兆苗錢市草千萬，俾民輸諸苑。

translations.literal: He also asked to use Jingzhao seed-money to buy ten million units of fodder and have the people deliver it to the imperial parks.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to use Jingzhao seed-money to buy ten million units of fodder and have the people deliver it to the imperial parks.

sentences.zh: 宰相陸贄等以為非是，不從。

translations.literal: The chief ministers Lu Zan and others held this wrong, and the emperor did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Ministers Lu Zan and others judged the plan unsound, and the emperor did not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 京右偏故有葦地數頃，延齡妄言：「長安、咸陽間，得陂艿數百頃，願以為內廄牧地，水甘草薦與苑廄等。」

translations.literal: On the western outskirts of the capital there were only a few acres of reed marsh; Yanling falsely reported: "Between Chang'an and Xianyang I have found several hundred acres of marsh pasture and wish to make it inner-stable grazing land, with water, fine grass, and fodder equal to the park stables.
translations.idiomatic: On the western outskirts of the capital there were only a few acres of reed marsh; Yanling falsely claimed: "Between Chang'an and Xianyang I have found several hundred acres of marsh pasture and wish to set it aside as inner-stable grazing land, with water, fine grass, and fodder to match the park stables.

sentences.zh: 帝信之，以問宰相，皆曰：「當無有。」

translations.literal: The emperor believed him and asked the chief ministers; all said: "There should be none."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him and asked the chief ministers; all replied: "There should be nothing of the kind."

sentences.zh: 帝遣使按覆，果詐。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to investigate and verify; it proved fraudulent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to investigate, and the claim proved fraudulent.

sentences.zh: 延齡大慚，帝不責也。

translations.literal: Yanling was deeply ashamed, but the emperor did not reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling was deeply ashamed, yet the emperor did not rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 京兆積歲和市不得直，尹李充請之官，延齡誣其妄，反令還輸，號曰「底折錢」。

translations.literal: For years Jingzhao's market purchases had failed to obtain fair value; the intendant Li Chong asked that the government take them over; Yanling slandered him as presumptuous and instead ordered repayment, calling it "bottom-discount money."
translations.idiomatic: For years Jingzhao's market purchases had failed to obtain fair prices; Intendant Li Chong asked the government to take them over; Yanling denounced him as presumptuous and instead ordered repayment, dubbing the sum "bottom-discount money."

sentences.zh: 嘗請斂財以實府，帝曰：「安得而實之？」

translations.literal: He once asked to gather funds to fill the treasury; the emperor said: "How can it be filled?
translations.idiomatic: He once asked to gather funds to fill the treasury; the emperor said, "How could it be filled?

sentences.zh: 延齡曰：「開元、天寶間，戶口繁息，百司務殷，官且有缺者。

translations.literal: Yanling said: "In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras the population flourished, the hundred offices were busy, and even offices had vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling replied: "Under Kaiyuan and Tianbao the population flourished, the hundred offices were busy, and even offices had vacancies.

sentences.zh: 比兵興，戶不半在，今一官治數司足矣。

translations.literal: Since warfare arose, not half the households remain; now one official can administer several bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, fewer than half the households remain; today one official can run several bureaus.

sentences.zh: 請後官闕不即補，收其稟以實帑簿。」

translations.literal: Please delay filling later vacancies and collect their salaries to fill the treasury ledgers."
translations.idiomatic: Let later vacancies go unfilled for a time and their salaries be collected to swell the treasury ledgers."

sentences.zh: 它日，帝謂延齡曰：「朕所居浴堂殿，一棟將壓，念易之，未能也。」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor said to Yanling: "The bath hall where I dwell—one beam is about to collapse; I think of replacing it but cannot.
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor told Yanling: "In the bath hall where I live, one beam is about to give way; I mean to replace it but cannot manage the cost.

sentences.zh: 延齡曰：「宗廟至重，殿棟微矣。

translations.literal: Yanling said: "The ancestral temple is supremely weighty; a hall beam is slight.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling said: "The ancestral temple is the weightiest concern of all; a hall beam is a trifling matter.

sentences.zh: 且陛下本分錢，用之亡窮，何所難哉？」

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has principal money—using it is inexhaustible; what could be difficult?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Your Majesty has principal money at your disposal—its use is inexhaustible; what could be difficult?"

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「本分錢奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said in surprise: "What is principal money?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in surprise, "What is this principal money?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此在經誼，愚儒不能知，臣能言之。

translations.literal: He answered: "This lies in canonical principle; foolish Confucians cannot know it, but your servant can explain it.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "This lies in canonical principle; foolish scholars cannot grasp it, but your servant can explain it.

sentences.zh: 按禮，天下賦三之：一以充乾豆，一以事賓客，一君之庖廚。

translations.literal: According to ritual, the empire's levies are divided in three: one to supply the dried meat vessels, one to serve guests, one for the ruler's kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, the empire's levies are divided in three: one third for the dried-meat vessels of sacrifice, one for receiving guests, and one for the ruler's kitchen.

sentences.zh: 陛下奉宗廟，能竭天下賦三之一乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty attends the ancestral temple—can you exhaust one third of the empire's levies?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty serves the ancestral temple—can you exhaust even one third of the empire's levies?

sentences.zh: 鴻臚禮賓，勞予四夷，用十一為有贏。

translations.literal: The Court of State Ceremonial receives guests and toils over the four barbarians—using one in ten leaves a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of State Ceremonial receives guests and toils over the four quarters—spending one part in ten still leaves a surplus.

sentences.zh: 陛下所禦饔餼簡儉，以所餘為百官稟料飧錢，未盡也，則所不盡者為本分錢。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's imperial meals are simple and frugal; what remains becomes the officials' salary grain and meal money; what is still not spent—that is principal money.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's imperial meals are plain and frugal; what remains goes to the officials' salary grain and meal allowances; what is still left over—that is principal money.

sentences.zh: 以治殿數十尚不乏，況一棟哉！」

translations.literal: To repair dozens of halls would still not exhaust it—how much less one beam!"
translations.idiomatic: To repair dozens of halls would scarcely exhaust it—how much less a single beam!"

sentences.zh: 帝頷曰：「人未嘗為朕言之。」

translations.literal: The emperor nodded and said: "No one has ever told me this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded and said, "No one has ever told me this before."

sentences.zh: 又造神龍佛祠，須材五十尺者。

translations.literal: He also built the Shenlong Buddhist shrine and needed timber fifty feet long.
translations.idiomatic: He also undertook construction of the Shenlong Buddhist shrine and needed timbers fifty feet long.

sentences.zh: 延齡妄奏：「同州得大谷，木數千章，度皆八十尺，」帝曰：「吾聞開元時，近山無巨木，求之嵐、勝間。

translations.literal: Yanling falsely memorialized: "In Tongzhou I have found a great valley with several thousand timbers, all measuring eighty feet"; the emperor said: "I have heard that in Kaiyuan times there were no great trees near the mountains, and they were sought between Lan and Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling falsely reported: "In Tong Prefecture I have found a great valley with several thousand timbers, each eighty feet long"; the emperor said, "I have heard that in Kaiyuan times there were no great trees near the mountains, and they had to be sought between Lan and Sheng.

sentences.zh: 今何地之近、材之良邪？」

translations.literal: What place is so near, what timber so fine?"
translations.idiomatic: What place is so near, and what timber so fine?"

sentences.zh: 延齡曰：「異材瑰產，處處有之，待聖主乃出。

translations.literal: Yanling said: "Rare timber and wondrous products exist everywhere; they wait for a sage ruler to bring them forth.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling said: "Rare timber and wondrous products exist everywhere; they wait for a sage ruler to bring them forth.

sentences.zh: 今生近輔，豈開元所當得也！」

translations.literal: Now they appear near the capital—how could Kaiyuan have obtained such!"
translations.idiomatic: Now they appear near the capital—how could the Kaiyuan era have obtained such!"

sentences.zh: 帝悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 是時，陸贄為宰相，帝素所信重，極論其譎妄不可任，帝以為排冒，愈益厚延齡。

translations.literal: At this time Lu Zan was chief minister, one the emperor had long trusted and honored; he argued at length that Yanling's deceit and presumption made him unfit for office, but the emperor took this as partisan attack and favored Yanling all the more.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Lu Zan was chief minister, a man the emperor had long trusted; he argued at length that Yanling's deceit and presumption made him unfit for office, but the emperor took this as partisan slander and favored Yanling all the more.

sentences.zh: 贄上疏列其狀，具言：「延齡嘗奏句獲乾隱二千萬緡，請舍別庫為羨余，供天子私費，故上之興作廣，宣索多矣。

translations.literal: Zan submitted a memorial listing his conduct in detail, stating fully: "Yanling once memorialized that he had uncovered two million strings in concealed dry goods, asked to set aside a separate storehouse as surplus, and supply the Son of Heaven's private expenses—hence the sovereign's construction grew vast and requisitions multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Zan submitted a memorial listing his conduct in detail, writing: "Yanling once reported that he had uncovered two million strings in concealed dry goods, asked to set aside a separate storehouse as surplus for the Son of Heaven's private expenses—hence the sovereign's building projects grew vast and requisitions multiplied.

sentences.zh: 延齡欲實其言，乃大搜市廛，奪所入獻，逮捕匠徒，迫脅就功，號曰『敕索』，弗仇其直，名曰『和雇』，弗與之庸。

translations.literal: Yanling wished to make his words real and therefore searched the markets broadly, seized what was brought in as tribute, arrested craftsmen and laborers, and coerced them to work—calling it "imperial requisition," refusing fair price and naming it "harmonious hire," yet giving no wages.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling wished to make good on his claim and therefore ransacked the markets, seized goods brought in as tribute, arrested craftsmen and laborers, and coerced them to work—calling it "imperial requisition," refusing fair price and naming it "harmonious hire," yet paying no wages.

sentences.zh: 又度支出納，與太府交相關制，出物旬計，見物月計，符按覆核，有御史以監董之，則財用不得回隱。

translations.literal: Moreover the revenue bureau's intake and outgo are mutually checked with the grand storehouse: outgoing goods are tallied every ten days, incoming goods every month, tally-slips are reviewed and verified, and censors supervise and inspect—so funds cannot be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the revenue bureau's intake and outgo are cross-checked with the grand storehouse: outgoing goods are tallied every ten days, incoming goods every month, tally-slips are reviewed and verified, and censors supervise inspection—so funds cannot be concealed.

sentences.zh: 延齡乃言掊糞土得銀十三萬兩，它貨且百萬，已棄而獲，皆羨余也，悉移舍以供別敕。

translations.literal: Yanling then said that digging in dung and earth yielded one hundred thirty thousand taels of silver and other goods nearing a million—all abandoned yet obtained, all surplus—and moved them entirely to supply separate imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling then claimed that digging in dung and earth yielded one hundred thirty thousand taels of silver and other goods nearing a million—all abandoned yet recovered, all surplus—and moved them entirely to supply separate imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 太府卿韋少華劾其妄，陛下縱之不為治，此乃侵削兆民，為天子取怨於下。」

translations.literal: The grand storehouse director Wei Shaohua impeached him for falsehood, yet Your Majesty indulged him and did not punish—this is to encroach upon and strip the myriad people and win resentment for the Son of Heaven below.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Storehouse Director Wei Shaohua impeached him for falsehood, yet Your Majesty indulged him and did not punish—this is to strip the myriad people and win resentment for the Son of Heaven among his subjects.

sentences.zh: 又引建中橫斂多積致播遷者，其言甚深切。

translations.literal: He also cited how the Jianzhong era's ruthless levies and vast accumulations had led to the court's exile—their words were very penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited how the ruthless levies and vast hoarding of the Jianzhong era had driven the court into exile—his words were piercing in their force.

sentences.zh: 帝得奏不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會鹽鐵使張滂、京兆尹李充、司農卿李铦皆指延齡專以險偽罔上，帝怒，乃罷贄宰相，左除滂等官。

translations.literal: It happened that the salt and iron commissioner Zhang Pang, the Jingzhao intendant Li Chong, and the minister of agriculture Li Xian all charged that Yanling relied solely on treacherous deceit to mislead the sovereign; the emperor grew angry, removed Zan from the chief ministership, and demoted Pang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Salt and Iron Commissioner Zhang Pang, Jingzhao Intendant Li Chong, and Minister of Agriculture Li Xian all charged that Yanling relied solely on treacherous deceit to mislead the throne; the emperor grew angry, removed Zan from the chief ministership, and demoted Pang and the others.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，人情愁惴。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought and the people's hearts were anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a great drought gripped the land, and the people were anxious and fearful.

sentences.zh: 延齡言：「贄等失權怨望，顯言歲饑民流、度支糧芻乏以激怒眾士。」

translations.literal: Yanling said: "Zan and the others, having lost power, resent and hope; they openly say the year is famine-struck, the people are fleeing, and the revenue bureau lacks grain and fodder—to inflame the crowd of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling said: "Zan and the others, having lost power, nurse resentment; they openly proclaim famine, fleeing populations, and shortages of grain and fodder at the revenue bureau—to inflame the scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 它日，帝畋苑中，而神策軍訴度支不賦廄芻者，天子惑延齡言，乃下詔斥逐贄等，朝廷震恐。

translations.literal: Another day, as the emperor hunted in the park, the Shence Army complained that the revenue bureau would not supply stable fodder; the Son of Heaven, swayed by Yanling's words, issued an edict expelling Zan and the others, and the court trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, as the emperor hunted in the park, the Shence Army complained that the revenue bureau would not supply stable fodder; swayed by Yanling's words, the Son of Heaven issued an edict expelling Zan and the others, and the court trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 延齡又捕充所善吏張忠榜掠之，誣充「沒官錢五十萬緡，以餌結權幸，令妻以犢車載金餉贄。」

translations.literal: Yanling also arrested Chong's favored clerk Zhang Zhong and tortured him under the cudgel, falsely charging Chong with "seizing five hundred thousand strings of official funds, using bait to win favor with the powerful, and having his wife load gold in a ox-cart to bribe Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling also arrested Chong's favored clerk Zhang Zhong and tortured him under the cudgel, falsely charging that Chong "had seized five hundred thousand strings of official funds, used bribes to win favor with the powerful, and had his wife load gold in an ox-cart to bribe Zan.

sentences.zh: 忠具獄，其母投訴光順門匭，有詔御史審劾，一夕得狀，乃釋忠。

translations.literal: Zhong furnished the full case; his mother lodged a complaint in the Guangshun Gate petition box; an edict ordered censors to investigate; in one night the truth was obtained, and Zhong was released.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong furnished the full case; his mother lodged a complaint in the Guangshun Gate petition box; an edict ordered the censors to investigate; within a single night the truth emerged, and Zhong was released.

sentences.zh: 延齡不得逞，復奏充妄用京兆錢谷，願下有司比句，以比部郎中崔元翰欲釋憾於贄也。

translations.literal: Yanling could not prevail and again memorialized that Chong had misused Jingzhao funds and grain, asking that subordinate offices compare accounts—because the director of comparisons Cui Yuanhan wished to vent resentment against Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling could not prevail and again memorialized that Chong had misused Jingzhao funds and grain, asking that subordinate offices audit the accounts—because Director of Comparisons Cui Yuanhan wished to vent his resentment against Zan.

sentences.zh: 賴刑部侍郎奚陟辨治，充等得不冤。

translations.literal: Thanks to Vice Minister of Justice Xi Zhi's clear adjudication, Chong and the others escaped wrongful conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Vice Minister of Justice Xi Zhi's clear adjudication, Chong and the others escaped wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 延齡資苛刻，又劫於利，專剝下附上，肆騁譎怪。

translations.literal: Yanling's nature was harsh and mean, and he was moreover driven by profit, specializing in stripping those below to please those above and giving free rein to deceit and strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling was harsh by nature and driven by greed, specializing in stripping those below to please those above and giving free rein to deceit and extravagance.

sentences.zh: 其進對，皆他人莫敢言，而延齡言之不疑，亦人之所未聞者。

translations.literal: In his audiences, what others dared not say he said without doubt, and also what men had never heard.
translations.idiomatic: In his audiences he spoke without hesitation of what others dared not say, and also of what men had never heard before.

sentences.zh: 帝頗知其詐，但以其不隱，欲聞外事，故斷用不疑。

translations.literal: The emperor knew fairly well that he was deceitful, but because he did not conceal himself and the emperor wished to hear outside affairs, he employed him decisively without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew fairly well that he was deceitful, but because he did not conceal himself and the emperor wished to hear news from outside the court, he employed him decisively without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 延齡恃得君，謂必輔政，少所降下，至嫚罵邇臣，時人側目。

translations.literal: Yanling relied on having won the ruler and believed he would surely assist in government, seldom lowering himself, even insulting and reviling nearby ministers—men of the time glared sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling, confident of the emperor's favor, believed he would surely rise to chief minister, seldom humbled himself, and even insulted nearby ministers—men of the time watched him with sidelong glances.

sentences.zh: 屬疾臥第，載度支官物輸之家，無敢言。

translations.literal: When he fell ill and lay at home, he loaded revenue-bureau goods into carts and delivered them to his house—no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill and lay at home, he loaded revenue-bureau goods into carts and delivered them to his house—no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 帝念之，使者日三輩往。

translations.literal: The emperor thought of him; envoys went three times a day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought constantly of him; envoys went three times a day.

sentences.zh: 死，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 人語以相安，唯帝悼不已。

translations.literal: People spoke of it to comfort one another; only the emperor mourned without end.
translations.idiomatic: People spoke of his death with relief; only the emperor mourned without end.

sentences.zh: 冊贈太子太傅、上柱國。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 永貞初，度支建言：「延齡曩列別庫，分藏正物，無實益而有吏文之煩。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzhen the revenue bureau proposed: "Yanling formerly set up separate storehouses and divided storage of regular goods—no real benefit, only clerical paperwork and trouble.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongzhen reign the revenue bureau proposed: "Yanling formerly set up separate storehouses and divided storage of regular goods—no real benefit, only clerical paperwork and trouble.

sentences.zh: 乃詔復以還左藏。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered that all be returned to the left treasury.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered that all be returned to the left treasury.

sentences.zh: 元和中，有司謚曰繆。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era the responsible offices gave the posthumous name "Deceptive."
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era the responsible offices gave him the posthumous name "Deceptive."

sentences.zh: 崔損，字至無，系本博陵。

translations.literal: Cui Sun, style name Zhiwu, was of the Boling lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Sun, whose style name was Zhiwu, came from the Boling lineage.

sentences.zh: 大歷間，中進士、博學宏辭，補校書郎、咸陽尉。

translations.literal: During the Dali era he passed the jinshi examination and the erudite examination in broad learning, and was appointed collator and Xianyang district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era he passed the jinshi examination and the erudite examination in broad learning, and was appointed collator and magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 避親，改大理評事。

translations.literal: To avoid a relative he was transferred to be an evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid serving under a relative he was transferred to an evaluator's post in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 累勞至右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service he reached Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated service he rose to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 於時，宰相趙憬卒，盧邁屬疾，裴延齡素善損，薦之德宗。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Minister Zhao Jing died and Lu Mai was afflicted with illness; Pei Yanling had long been on good terms with Sun and recommended him to Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Minister Zhao Jing died and Lu Mai fell ill; Pei Yanling had long been on good terms with Sun and recommended him to Dezong.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年，以本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he was made, in his present office, Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In 796 he was made, while retaining his present office, Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 始，中書虛位十日，議者謂選有德，及用損，中外悵失。

translations.literal: At first the Secretariat had been vacant ten days; commentators said a man of virtue would be chosen—when Sun was appointed, court and country alike were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat had stood vacant for ten days; commentators expected a man of virtue to be chosen—when Sun was appointed, court and country alike were disappointed.

sentences.zh: 而損性齪齪能自將，延英進見，不敢出一言及天下事。

translations.literal: Yet Sun's nature was cautious and self-restrained; in Yanying audiences he dared not utter a single word touching affairs under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sun was cautious and self-restrained by nature; in Yanying audiences he dared not utter a single word on affairs under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 逾年，進門下侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was advanced to vice-minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was advanced to vice-minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 嘗以疾臥家久，賜絹三百為醫藥費。

translations.literal: Once, when he lay ill at home for a long time, he was granted three hundred bolts of silk for medical expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he lay ill at home for a long time, he was granted three hundred bolts of silk for medical expenses.

sentences.zh: 損無卓卓稱於人者，而歷二省華要至宰相。

translations.literal: Sun had no outstanding reputation among men, yet passed through the two ministries' splendid posts to chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sun had won no outstanding reputation among men, yet passed through the splendid posts of both ministries to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 母殯而不葬，亦不展殯；

translations.literal: His mother's coffin lay unburied, and he did not even extend the mourning display;
translations.idiomatic: His mother's coffin lay unburied, and he did not even observe the mourning display;

sentences.zh: 女兄為尼，沒不臨喪。

translations.literal: his elder sister became a nun, and when she died he did not attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: his elder sister became a nun, and when she died he did not attend her funeral.

sentences.zh: 建中後，宰相無久任者，損以便柔遜願中帝意，乃留八年。

translations.literal: After Jianzhong no chief minister held office long; Sun, by being accommodating, soft, and deferential to hit the emperor's intent, remained eight years.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jianzhong era no chief minister held office long; Sun, by being accommodating, soft, and deferential enough to please the emperor, remained in post for eight years.

sentences.zh: 帝亦知公議病其持祿，然憐遇彌渥。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew that public opinion faulted him for holding salary, yet treated him with ever greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also knew that public opinion faulted him for clinging to office and salary, yet treated him with ever greater favor.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太傅，謚曰靖。

translations.literal: He died; was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name "Tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name "Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 韋渠牟，京兆萬年人，工部侍郎述從子也。

translations.literal: Wei Qumou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, a nephew of the vice-minister of works Wei Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qumou came from Wannian in Jingzhao and was a nephew of Vice-Minister of Works Wei Shu.

sentences.zh: 少警悟，工為詩，李白異之，授以古樂府。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick-witted, skilled at poetry; Li Bai thought him unusual and taught him ancient yuefu.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and skilled at poetry; Li Bai took notice of him and taught him ancient yuefu verse.

sentences.zh: 去為道士，不終，更為浮屠，已而復冠。

translations.literal: He left to become a Daoist priest but did not finish; he then became a Buddhist monk, and afterward put on the cap again.
translations.idiomatic: He left to become a Daoist priest but did not stay; he then became a Buddhist monk, and afterward returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 浙西韓滉表試校書郎，進至四門博士。

translations.literal: Han Huang of Zhexi recommended him for trial appointment as collator, and he advanced to Erudite of the Four Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang of Western Zhe recommended him for trial appointment as collator, and he rose to Erudite of the Four Gates.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年，德宗誕日，詔給事中徐岱、兵部郎中趙需、禮部郎中許孟容與渠牟及佛老二師並對麟德殿，質問大趣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan, on Dezong's birthday, an edict ordered Supervising Secretary Xu Dai, Director of the Board of War Zhao Xu, Director of the Board of Rites Xu Mengrong, Qumou, and two masters of Buddhism and Daoism to face one another in the Linde Hall and debate the great principles.
translations.idiomatic: In 796, on Dezong's birthday, an edict ordered Supervising Secretary Xu Dai, Director of the Board of War Zhao Xu, Director of the Board of Rites Xu Mengrong, Qumou, and two masters of Buddhism and Daoism to debate one another in the Linde Hall on the great principles.

sentences.zh: 渠牟有口辯，雖於三家未究解，然答問鋒生，帝聽之意動。

translations.literal: Qumou had eloquence; though he had not thoroughly mastered the three teachings, his replies in debate were sharp, and as the emperor listened his mind was stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Qumou was eloquent; though he had not mastered the three teachings in depth, his replies were sharp in debate, and as the emperor listened his mind was stirred.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書郎，進詩七百言。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretary; he presented a poem of seven hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary and presented a poem of seven hundred lines.

sentences.zh: 未浹旬，擢右補闕內供奉。

translations.literal: Before ten days had passed he was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor with inner attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than ten days he was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor with inner attendance.

sentences.zh: 始，同列易之，後數遣中人專召渠牟，由是皆屬目。

translations.literal: At first his colleagues looked down on him; later the emperor repeatedly sent eunuchs to summon Qumou alone, and thereby all turned their eyes to him.
translations.idiomatic: At first his colleagues looked down on him; later the emperor repeatedly sent eunuchs to summon Qumou alone, and thereby all turned their eyes to him.

sentences.zh: 歲中，至諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Within the year he reached Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he rose to Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 大抵延英對，雖大臣率漏下二三刻止，渠牟每奏事，輒五六刻乃罷，天子歡甚。

translations.literal: Generally in Yanying audiences, even great ministers usually ended when the water clock ran two or three marks past; whenever Qumou reported affairs it took five or six marks before stopping, and the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, Yanying audiences ended two or three marks past the hour even for great ministers; whenever Qumou reported affairs the session lasted five or six marks, and the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 渠牟為人佻躁，志向浮淺，不根於道德仁義，特用憸巧中帝意，非有嘉謨正辭感悟得君也。

translations.literal: Qumou as a man was frivolous and rash, his aims shallow, not rooted in morality and benevolence-righteousness; he relied solely on crafty flattery to hit the emperor's intent—not on excellent counsel and upright words to move and win the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Qumou was frivolous and rash by nature, shallow in purpose, and ungrounded in morality and benevolent duty; he won the emperor solely through crafty flattery, not through excellent counsel and upright words that might truly move the throne.

sentences.zh: 自陸贄免，帝躬攬庶政，不復委權於下。

translations.literal: From the time Lu Zan was removed, the emperor personally took hold of common government and no longer delegated power below.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Zan was removed, the emperor personally took hold of routine government and no longer delegated power below.

sentences.zh: 宰相取充位、行文書而已，至守宰、御史，皆自推簡。

translations.literal: Chief ministers merely filled posts and transmitted documents; as for prefects, magistrates, and censors, the emperor himself made selections.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers merely filled posts and transmitted documents; as for prefects, magistrates, and censors, the emperor himself made the selections.

sentences.zh: 然處深宮，所倚而信者裴延齡、李齊運、王紹、李實、韋執誼與渠牟等，其權侔人主。

translations.literal: Yet dwelling deep in the palace, those he relied on and trusted—Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, Wang Shao, Li Shi, Wei Zhiyi, and Qumou among others—their power equaled the sovereign's.
translations.idiomatic: Yet dwelling deep in the palace, those he relied on and trusted—Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, Wang Shao, Li Shi, Wei Zhiyi, and Qumou among others—wielded power equal to the sovereign's.

sentences.zh: 延齡、實皆奸虐，紹無所建明。

translations.literal: Yanling and Shi were both treacherous and cruel; Shao had nothing to establish or clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling and Shi were both treacherous and cruel; Shao accomplished nothing of note.

sentences.zh: 渠牟後出，望最輕，張恩勢以動天下，召崔芋於茅山，超鄭隨布衣至補闕，引醴泉令馮伉為給事中、太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Qumou came out later, his reputation the lightest; he spread favor and power to shake the empire, summoned Cui Yu from Maoshan, promoted Zheng Sui from commoner to supplementation censor, and brought in Liquan magistrate Feng Kang as supervising secretary and tutor to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Qumou rose later and carried the lightest reputation; he spread favor and power to shake the empire, summoned Cui Yu from Mount Mao, promoted Zheng Sui from commoner to supplementation censor, and brought in Liquan Magistrate Feng Kang as supervising secretary and tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 帝既偏於任聽，士之浮競甘進者爭出其門，赫然勢焰可炙。

translations.literal: Since the emperor was partial in appointment and listening, scholars who were frivolous, competitive, and eager to advance all vied to pass through his gate; his blazing power could scorch one.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor was partial in whom he appointed and heard, scholars who were frivolous, competitive, and eager to advance all vied to pass through his gate; his blazing influence could scorch one.

sentences.zh: 再擢太常卿。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十三，贈刑部尚書，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-three; was posthumously made Minister of Justice, with the posthumous name "Loyal."
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously made Minister of Justice, with the posthumous name "Loyal."

sentences.zh: 所論著甚多，傳於時。

translations.literal: His writings and discussions were many and circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were many and circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 李齊運者，蔣王惲孫。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun was a grandson of Prince of Jiang, Li Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun was a grandson of Prince of Jiang, Li Yun.

sentences.zh: 始補寧王府東閣祭酒，擢累監察御史，復辟江淮都統李亙府。

translations.literal: He first filled the post of eastern-pavilion libationer in the Prince of Ning's household, was promoted in succession to investigating censor, and again entered the staff of the Jiang-Huai overall commander Li Gen.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as eastern-pavilion libationer in the Prince of Ning's household, rose in succession to investigating censor, and again entered the staff of Jiang-Huai Overall Commander Li Gen.

sentences.zh: 由工部郎中為長安令，政頗修辦。

translations.literal: From director of the Board of Works he became magistrate of Chang'an; his administration was fairly well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: From director of the Board of Works he became magistrate of Chang'an; his administration was fairly well ordered.

sentences.zh: 宗正少卿李瀚從子有所訟，齊運於瀚為卑行，而不禮訟者。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Li Han's nephew brought a suit; Qiyun, being Han's junior in clan rank, showed no courtesy to the litigant.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Li Han's nephew brought a suit; Qiyun, being Han's junior in clan rank, showed no courtesy to the litigant.

sentences.zh: 瀚怒，辱諸朝，齊運以聞，代宗貶瀚。

translations.literal: Han grew angry and insulted him at court; Qiyun reported it, and Daizong demoted Han.
translations.idiomatic: Han grew angry and insulted him at court; Qiyun reported it, and Daizong demoted Han.

sentences.zh: 由是稍擢京兆少尹。

translations.literal: Thereby he was gradually promoted to vice-intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he was gradually promoted to vice-intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 出為河中尹、晉絳慈隰觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as intendant of Hezhong and military commissioner of Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as intendant of Hezhong and military commissioner of Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 德宗出狩，李懷光還兵奔難，晝夜馳，及河中，士罷困，乃休三日。

translations.literal: When Dezong went out on campaign, Li Huaiguang turned his army back to rush to the crisis, galloping day and night; when he reached Hezhong the troops were exhausted and he rested three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong went out on campaign, Li Huaiguang turned his army back to rush to the crisis, galloping day and night; when he reached Hezhong the troops were exhausted and he rested three days.

sentences.zh: 齊運悉所賦勞軍，牛酒豐甘，人人喜悅。

translations.literal: Qiyun levied everything he could to reward the army; beef and wine were rich and sweet, and every man was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun levied everything he could to reward the army; beef and wine were rich and sweet, and every man was pleased.

sentences.zh: 及懷光反，還守河中，齊運棄城走。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang rebelled and returned to hold Hezhong, Qiyun abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiguang rebelled and returned to hold Hezhong, Qiyun abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Jingzhao intendant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Jingzhao intendant.

sentences.zh: 時李晟壁渭橋，齊運發民築城保，督芻粟以餉晟。

translations.literal: At the time Li Sheng was encamped at the Wei Bridge; Qiyun mobilized the people to build fortifications and supervised fodder and grain to supply Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Sheng was encamped at the Wei Bridge; Qiyun mobilized the people to build fortifications and supervised fodder and grain to supply Sheng.

sentences.zh: 賊平，頗有助。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he had contributed considerably.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified he had contributed considerably.

sentences.zh: 萬年丞源邃不事，齊運怒，捽辱之，死於廷。

translations.literal: Wannian assistant magistrate Yuan Sui would not serve him; Qiyun grew angry, seized and humiliated him, and he died in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian Assistant Magistrate Yuan Sui would not serve him; Qiyun grew angry, seized and humiliated him, and Yuan died in the hall.

sentences.zh: 邃家告冤，御史大夫崔縱請窮治，帝不許。

translations.literal: Sui's family reported the injustice; Censor-in-Chief Cui Zong asked for thorough punishment, but the emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's family reported the injustice; Censor-in-Chief Cui Zong asked for thorough punishment, but the emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 御史聯章深劾，齊運訴於帝，言為朋黨所擠。

translations.literal: Censors submitted joint memorials impeaching him deeply; Qiyun appealed to the emperor, saying he was squeezed by faction.
translations.idiomatic: Censors submitted joint memorials impeaching him deeply; Qiyun appealed to the emperor, saying he was squeezed by faction.

sentences.zh: 天子使宰相諭諫官御史，後毋得群署章以劾，然卒不直邃冤。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had the chief minister instruct remonstrators and censors that thereafter they must not jointly sign memorials to impeach; yet in the end Sui's injustice was not vindicated.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven had the chief minister instruct remonstrators and censors that thereafter they must not jointly sign memorials to impeach; yet in the end Sui's injustice was never vindicated.

sentences.zh: 久之，大蝗旱，齊運不能政，乃以韓洄代之，改宗正卿、閑廄宮苑使。

translations.literal: After a long time there were great locusts and drought; Qiyun could not govern, and Han Hui was made to replace him; he was changed to Director of the Imperial Clan and commissioner of idle stables and palace parks.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time there were great locusts and drought; Qiyun could not govern, and Han Hui was made to replace him; he was reassigned as Director of the Imperial Clan and commissioner of idle stables and palace parks.

sentences.zh: 進至禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He advanced to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 宰相內殿對已，齊運常次進，帝與參決大事。

translations.literal: After the chief ministers had finished audience in the inner hall, Qiyun usually entered next, and the emperor discussed and decided great affairs with him.
translations.idiomatic: After the chief ministers had finished audience in the inner hall, Qiyun usually entered next, and the emperor discussed and decided great affairs with him.

sentences.zh: 既無學，暗於大體，第以甘言阿匼而已。

translations.literal: He had no learning and was blind to the great pattern; he merely used sweet words and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: He had no learning and was blind to the great pattern; he merely used sweet words and flattery.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦李锜為浙西，受賂數十萬，又薦李詞為湖州刺史，人告其贓，帝置不問。

translations.literal: He once recommended Li Qi for Zhexi and received bribes of several hundred thousand; he also recommended Li Ci as prefect of Huzhou—when men reported his corruption the emperor set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended Li Qi for Western Zhe and received bribes of several hundred thousand; he also recommended Li Ci as prefect of Hu Prefecture—when men reported his corruption the emperor set it aside without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 齊運臥疾，滿歲不能謁，每除吏，往往遣使即家咨逮。

translations.literal: Qiyun lay ill a full year unable to attend audience; whenever an official was appointed he often sent envoys to his home to consult and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun lay ill a full year unable to attend audience; whenever an official was appointed he often sent envoys to his home to consult and decide.

sentences.zh: 晚以妾為妻，具冕服行禮，士人蚩之。

translations.literal: Late in life he made a concubine his wife, furnished cap and robes, and performed the rites—scholars mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he made a concubine his wife, furnished cap and robes, and performed the rites—scholars mocked him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-two; was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 李實，道王元慶四世孫。

translations.literal: Li Shi was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince of Dao, Li Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince of Dao, Li Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 以蔭仕，嗣曹王臯辟署江西府判官，遷蘄州刺史。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he entered service; the Prince of Cao, Li Gao, recruited him as Jiangxi judicial aide, and he was transferred to prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he entered service; Prince of Cao Li Gao recruited him as Jiangxi judicial aide, and he was transferred to prefect of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 臯節度山南東道，復從之。

translations.literal: When Gao governed the Shannan East circuit, he again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao governed the Shannan East circuit, he again followed him.

sentences.zh: 臯卒，實知後務，刻薄軍費，士怨怒，欲殺之，夜縋亡歸京師。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Shi took charge of subsequent affairs, was harsh in cutting military expenses, the troops resented and raged and wished to kill him; he was lowered by rope at night and fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, Shi took charge of subsequent affairs, was harsh in cutting military expenses, the troops resented and raged and wished to kill him; he was lowered by rope at night and fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 累進司農卿，擢拜京兆尹，封嗣道王。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Minister of Agriculture, then appointed Jingzhao intendant and enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Minister of Agriculture, then appointed Jingzhao intendant and enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Dao.

sentences.zh: 怙寵而愎，不循法度。

translations.literal: Relying on favor he was obstinate and did not follow law and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on favor he was obstinate and did not follow law and regulation.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十年旱，關輔饑，實方務聚斂以結恩，民訴府上，一不問。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenyuan there was drought; the Guanfu region was famine-struck; Shi was then bent on gathering wealth to win favor—the people appealed to the prefecture and he did not inquire once.
translations.idiomatic: In 804 there was drought; the Guanfu region was famine-struck; Shi was then bent on gathering wealth to win favor—the people appealed to the prefecture and he did not inquire once.

sentences.zh: 德宗訪外疾苦，實詭曰：「歲雖旱，不害有秋。」

translations.literal: Dezong inquired into outside suffering; Shi deceitfully said: "Though the year is drought-struck, it does not harm the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong inquired into suffering outside the palace; Shi deceitfully said, "Though the year is drought-struck, it does not harm the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 乃峻責租調，人窮無告，至徹舍鬻苗輸於官。

translations.literal: He then harshly exacted rent and tax; people were destitute with nowhere to appeal, even tearing down houses and selling seedlings to deliver to the government.
translations.idiomatic: He then harshly exacted rent and tax; people were destitute with nowhere to appeal, even tearing down houses and selling seedlings to deliver to the government.

sentences.zh: 優人成輔端為俳語諷帝，實怒，奏賤工謗國，帝為殺之。

translations.literal: The actor Cheng Fuduan made comic lines to satirize the emperor; Shi grew angry and memorialized that a base craftsman had slandered the state; the emperor had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The actor Cheng Fuduan made comic lines to satirize the emperor; Shi grew angry and memorialized that a base craftsman had slandered the state; the emperor had him killed.

sentences.zh: 或言：「古者，瞽誦箴諫，雖恢諧托諭，何誅焉？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "In antiquity blind singers recited admonitions; though broad humor conveyed instruction, why execute them?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "In antiquity blind singers recited admonitions; though broad humor conveyed instruction, why execute them?

sentences.zh: 帝悔，然不罪實。

translations.literal: The emperor regretted it, yet did not punish Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted it, yet did not punish Shi.

sentences.zh: 故事，京兆避臺官。

translations.literal: By precedent Jingzhao yielded to censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent Jingzhao yielded to censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 實嘗與御史王播遇，而騶唱爭道。

translations.literal: Shi once met the censor Wang Bo, and their outriders' announcements disputed the road.
translations.idiomatic: Shi once met Censor Wang Bo, and their outriders' announcements disputed the road.

sentences.zh: 播鉤責從者，實怒，奏播為三原令，廷辱之。

translations.literal: Bo hooked and blamed the followers; Shi grew angry, memorialized to make Bo magistrate of Sanyuan, and humiliated him in court.
translations.idiomatic: Bo hooked and blamed the followers; Shi grew angry, memorialized to make Bo magistrate of Sanyuan, and humiliated him in court.

sentences.zh: 惡萬年令李眾，誣逐虔州司馬，以所善虞部員外郎房啟代之。

translations.literal: He hated Wannian magistrate Li Zhong, falsely drove him out as prefectural aide in Qianzhou, and replaced him with his favorite outer-office member of the Board of Parks Fang Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He hated Wannian Magistrate Li Zhong, falsely drove him out as prefectural aide in Qian Prefecture, and replaced him with his favorite outer-office member of the Board of Parks Fang Qi.

sentences.zh: 其怙權作威若此。

translations.literal: His relying on power and making might were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way he relied on power and made a show of might.

sentences.zh: 公卿為讒短遷斥者甚眾，專情謷色見顏間。

translations.literal: Many among the dukes and ministers were slandered and transferred or expelled; he specialized in arrogant looks that showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Many among the dukes and ministers were slandered and transferred or expelled; he specialized in arrogant looks that showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 權德輿為禮部，而實私薦士二十人，迫語曰：「應用此第，不爾，君且外遷！」

translations.literal: Quan Deyu was in the Board of Rites, yet Shi privately recommended twenty candidates and coerced him, saying: "You must use this rank—otherwise you will soon be transferred out!
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu was in the Board of Rites, yet Shi privately recommended twenty candidates and coerced him, saying, "You must use this rank—otherwise you will soon be transferred out!

sentences.zh: 德輿雖拒之，然常憚其誣。

translations.literal: Deyu though he refused still constantly feared his slander.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu refused, yet still constantly feared his slander.

sentences.zh: 吏部每奏科目頗嚴密，以杜請托，實公詣曹劫請趙宗儒，無所畏。

translations.literal: Whenever the Board of Personnel reported examination subjects it was fairly strict to block patronage; Shi openly went to the bureau to coerce Zhao Zongru without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Board of Personnel reported examination subjects it was fairly strict to block patronage; Shi openly went to the bureau to coerce Zhao Zongru without fear.

sentences.zh: 詔書蠲人逋租，實格詔固斂，畿民大困，官吏皆被榜罰，掊取二十萬緡。

translations.literal: An edict remitted people's overdue rent; Shi blocked the edict and still collected firmly; the capital-region people were greatly distressed; officials were all flogged and fined, and twenty million strings were extorted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict remitted people's overdue rent; Shi blocked the edict and still collected firmly; the capital-region people were greatly distressed; officials were all flogged and fined, and twenty million strings were extorted.

sentences.zh: 吏乞貸豪厘，輒死。

translations.literal: When clerks begged to borrow the smallest amount they were at once killed.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks begged to borrow the smallest amount they were at once killed.

sentences.zh: 按之無罪者，猥曰「死亦非枉」，復殺之。

translations.literal: Those investigated and found guiltless he roughly said "even death would not be wrongful" and killed them again.
translations.idiomatic: Those investigated and found guiltless he would say "even death would not be wrongful" and kill them anyway.

sentences.zh: 專以殘忍為政。

translations.literal: He specialized in cruelty as government.
translations.idiomatic: He governed solely through cruelty.

sentences.zh: 順宗在諒暗，不逾月，實殺數十人於府。

translations.literal: While Shunzong was in mourning seclusion, within less than a month Shi killed dozens of men in the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While Shunzong was in mourning seclusion, within less than a month Shi killed dozens of men in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貶通州長史。

translations.literal: He was demoted to chief administrator of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to chief administrator of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 市人爭懷瓦石邀劫之，實懼，夜遁去，長安中相賀。

translations.literal: Market people vied to carry tiles and stones to waylay and rob him; Shi was afraid and fled by night; in Chang'an all congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Market people vied to carry tiles and stones to waylay and rob him; Shi was afraid and fled by night; in Chang'an all congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 以赦令內移，死虢州。

translations.literal: By amnesty he was moved inward and died in Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: By amnesty he was moved inward and died in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 皇甫镈，涇州臨涇人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo was a native of Linjing in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo came from Linjing in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，第進士，又擢制科，為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he passed the jinshi examination, was also selected in the special examination, and became investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan reign he passed the jinshi examination, was also selected in the special examination, and became investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 居喪遊處不度，下除詹事府司直。

translations.literal: During mourning his conduct was unrestrained; he was demoted to rectifier in the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning his conduct was unrestrained; he was demoted to rectifier in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷吏部員外郎，典南曹，鈐制吏奸，稍知名。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to outer-office member of the Board of Personnel, managed the southern bureau, restrained clerical corruption, and gradually became known.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was transferred to outer-office member of the Board of Personnel, managed the southern bureau, restrained clerical corruption, and gradually became known.

sentences.zh: 進郎中，遷累司農卿，判度支，改戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He advanced to director, was transferred in succession to Minister of Agriculture, concurrently judged the revenue bureau, and was changed to vice-minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to director, was transferred in succession to Minister of Agriculture, concurrently judged the revenue bureau, and was changed to vice-minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 憲宗方伐蔡，急於用度，镈裒會嚴亟，以辦濟師，帝悅，進兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Xianzong was then campaigning against Cai and urgent for funds; Bo gathered and tallied with harsh speed to supply the army; the emperor was pleased and advanced him to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was then campaigning against Cai and urgent for funds; Bo gathered and tallied with harsh speed to supply the army; the emperor was pleased and advanced him to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 蔡平之明年，遂同中書門下平章事，猶領度支。

translations.literal: The year after Cai was pacified he became Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, still heading the revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The year after Cai was pacified he became Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, still heading the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 镈以吏道進，既由聚斂句剝為宰相，至雖市道皆嗤之。

translations.literal: Bo advanced through the clerical path; having become chief minister through gathering wealth and exacting accounts, even the marketplace sneered at him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo advanced through the clerical path; having become chief minister through gathering wealth and exacting accounts, even the marketplace sneered at him.

sentences.zh: 崔群、裴度以聞，帝怒，不聽。

translations.literal: Cui Qun and Pei Du reported it; the emperor grew angry and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun and Pei Du reported it; the emperor grew angry and would not listen.

sentences.zh: 度乃表罷政事，極論镈奸邪苛刻，天下怨之，將食其肉。

translations.literal: Du then memorialized to resign from government, arguing at length that Bo was treacherous, evil, and harsh, that the empire resented him and would eat his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Du then memorialized to resign from government, arguing at length that Bo was treacherous, evil, and harsh, that the empire resented him and would eat his flesh.

sentences.zh: 且言：「天下安否系朝廷，朝廷輕重在輔相。

translations.literal: He also said: "Whether the empire is secure or not depends on the court; the court's weight and lightness depend on the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Whether the empire is secure or not depends on the court; the court's weight and lightness depend on the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 今承宗削地，程權赴闕，韓弘輿疾討賊，非力能制之，顧朝廷處置能服其心也。

translations.literal: Now Chengzong has surrendered territory, Cheng Quan has come to court, Han Hong, though ill in his carriage, attacks the rebels—not because force alone can control them, but because they look to whether the court's handling can win their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chengzong has surrendered territory, Cheng Quan has come to court, and Han Hong, though ill in his carriage, attacks the rebels—not because force alone can control them, but because they look to whether the court's handling can win their hearts.

sentences.zh: 若相镈，則四方解矣。

translations.literal: If Bo is made chief minister, the four quarters will lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: If Bo is made chief minister, the four quarters will lose heart.

sentences.zh: 請授以浙西觀察使。」

translations.literal: Please appoint him military commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Please appoint him military commissioner of Western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 其辭切至。

translations.literal: His words were penetrating and extreme.
translations.idiomatic: His words were penetrating and forceful.

sentences.zh: 帝以天下略平，亦欲崇臺沼宮觀自娛樂，镈與程異知帝意，故數貢羨財，陰佐所欲，又賂吐突承璀為奧援。

translations.literal: The emperor, since the empire was largely pacified, also wished to elevate terraces, ponds, and palace temples for his own pleasure; Bo and Cheng Yi knew the emperor's intent and therefore repeatedly presented surplus funds, secretly aiding what he desired, and also bribed Tufa Chenghui as a hidden support.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, since the empire was largely pacified, also wished to elevate terraces, ponds, and palace temples for his own pleasure; Bo and Cheng Yi knew the emperor's intent and therefore repeatedly presented surplus funds, secretly aiding what he desired, and also bribed Tufa Chenghui as a hidden support.

sentences.zh: 故帝排眾論，決任之，反以度為朋黨，不內其言。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor set aside public opinion and resolved to employ him, instead treating Du as a faction and not taking in his words.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperor set aside public opinion and resolved to employ him, instead treating Du as a faction and not taking in his words.

sentences.zh: 镈乃益以巧媚自固，建損內外官稟佐國用，給事中崔植上還詔書，乃止。

translations.literal: Bo then all the more used crafty flattery to secure himself, proposing to cut inner and outer officials' salaries to assist state expenses; Supervising Secretary Cui Zhi returned the edict draft and only then was it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bo then all the more used crafty flattery to secure himself, proposing to cut inner and outer officials' salaries to assist state expenses; Supervising Secretary Cui Zhi returned the edict draft and only then was it stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝斥內帑所餘，詔度支評直，镈貴售之以給邊兵，故繒陳彩，觸手輒壞，士怨怒，聚焚之。

translations.literal: The emperor released surplus from the inner treasury and ordered the revenue bureau to appraise fair value; Bo sold it at high price to supply border troops—old piled silk and brocade broke at a touch; soldiers resented and raged and gathered to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released surplus from the inner treasury and ordered the revenue bureau to appraise fair value; Bo sold it at high price to supply border troops—old piled silk and brocade broke at a touch; soldiers resented and raged and gathered to burn it.

sentences.zh: 裴度以其事聞，镈指所著靴曰：「此內府所出，牢韌可服，彼言不可用，詐也。」

translations.literal: Pei Du reported the matter; Bo pointed to the boots he wore and said: "These come from the inner storehouse, firm and durable and fit to wear—those who say they cannot be used are deceiving.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du reported the matter; Bo pointed to the boots he wore and said, "These come from the inner storehouse, firm and durable and fit to wear—those who say they cannot be used are deceiving.

sentences.zh: 帝信之。

translations.literal: The emperor believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 镈銜度，乃與李逢吉、令狐楚合擠之，出度太原。

translations.literal: Bo harbored resentment against Du and therefore joined Li Fengji and Linghu Chu to squeeze him out, sending Du to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bo harbored resentment against Du and therefore joined Li Fengji and Linghu Chu to squeeze him out, sending Du to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 又以崔群有天下重望，勁正敢言，後議帝號，镈乃譖群抑損徽稱。

translations.literal: Also, since Cui Qun had heavy reputation throughout the empire, was firm, upright, and daring in speech, and later debated the emperor's posthumous title, Bo slandered that Qun had diminished the august designation.
translations.idiomatic: Also, since Cui Qun had heavy reputation throughout the empire, was firm, upright, and daring in speech, and later debated the emperor's posthumous title, Bo slandered that Qun had diminished the august designation.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逐群湖南。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and banished Qun to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and sent Qun into exile in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 镈罷度支，進門下侍郎平章事。

translations.literal: Bo was removed from the revenue bureau and advanced to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Bo relinquished control of the revenue bureau and was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery with the title of Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 嘗與金吾將軍李道古共薦方士柳泌、浮屠大通為長年藥，帝惑之。

translations.literal: He once joined the Gold Crow Guard general Li Daogu in recommending the adept Liu Bi and the Buddhist monk Datong for longevity elixirs, and the emperor was deluded.
translations.idiomatic: He had once joined Gold Crow Guard General Li Daogu in recommending the alchemist Liu Bi and the Buddhist monk Datong as makers of elixirs of long life, and the emperor was taken in.

sentences.zh: 穆宗在東宮，聞其奸妄，始聽政，集群臣於月華門，貶镈崖州司戶參軍，死其所。

translations.literal: Muzong, while in the Eastern Palace, heard of their treachery and imposture; when he first took the reins of government, he gathered the ministers at the Moon Hua Gate, demoted Bo to prefectural aide in Yazhou, and he died there.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, Muzong had heard of their fraud and imposture; as soon as he began to rule, he assembled the court at the Moon Hua Gate, demoted Bo to prefectural aide in Yazhou, where Bo died.

sentences.zh: 泌者，本楊仁晝也，習方伎。

translations.literal: Bi was originally Yang Renzhou and was versed in occult arts.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had originally been named Yang Renzhou and was trained in occult arts.

sentences.zh: 道古薦於镈，召入禁中，自雲能致藥為不死者，因言：「天臺山靈仙所舍，多異草，願官天臺，求采之。」

translations.literal: Daogu recommended him to Bo; he was summoned into the inner palace and declared himself able to obtain drugs that made one undying, then said: "Mount Tiantai is where numinous immortals dwell, and many strange herbs grow there; I wish to be appointed to Tiantai to seek and gather them.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu recommended him to Bo, and he was summoned into the palace, claiming he could produce drugs that would grant immortality. He then said, "Mount Tiantai is the dwelling place of divine immortals, and many rare herbs grow there. I ask to be made prefect of Tiantai so that I may gather them.

sentences.zh: 起徒步拜臺州刺史，賜金紫。

translations.literal: From commoner status on foot he was appointed prefect of Taizhou and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from commoner status to be appointed prefect of Taizhou and was granted the gold seal and purple robe of high rank.

sentences.zh: 諫臣固爭，以為列聖亦有寵方士，未嘗使牧民，帝曰：「煩一州而致長年於君父，何愛哉？」

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials argued firmly, saying that successive emperors had also favored adepts but had never made them govern the people; the emperor said: "To trouble one prefecture in order to bring long life to one's lord and father—what is there to regret?
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials protested vigorously, noting that previous emperors had favored adepts too but had never put them in charge of governing the people. The emperor replied, "What is one prefecture, if it can bring long life to one's lord and father? Why hesitate?

sentences.zh: 後不敢言。

translations.literal: Afterward none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no one dared object further.

sentences.zh: 泌驅吏民采藥山谷間，鞭笞苛急，歲餘無所獲。

translations.literal: Bi drove officials and commoners to gather drugs in mountain valleys, whipping them harshly and urgently; after more than a year he obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Bi drove officials and commoners into the mountain valleys to gather herbs, lashing them with merciless severity, yet after more than a year he had found nothing.

sentences.zh: 懼詐窮，舉族遁去，浙東觀察使捕得。

translations.literal: Fearing that his fraud was exhausted, he fled with his whole clan; the military commissioner of Eastern Zhe captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, he fled with his entire clan, but the military commissioner of Eastern Zhe captured him.

sentences.zh: 镈與道古營解，乃復待詔翰林。

translations.literal: Bo and Daogu worked to secure his release, and he was again made a Hanlin attendant awaiting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Bo and Daogu interceded on his behalf, and he was restored to the Hanlin Academy as an attendant awaiting edicts.

sentences.zh: 帝餌泌藥，浸躁怒不常，宦侍懼，以弒崩。

translations.literal: The emperor took Bi's drug, gradually grew irritable and unpredictable in anger, the eunuch attendants feared, and he died by assassination.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Bi's elixir and gradually grew irritable and unpredictable; the eunuch attendants grew afraid, and the emperor was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 大通自言百五十歲，镈敗，與泌皆誅。

translations.literal: Datong claimed for himself one hundred fifty years; when Bo fell, both he and Bi were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Datong claimed to be one hundred fifty years old; when Bo fell from power, both he and Bi were put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，吏責泌妄，答曰：「皆道古教我。」

translations.literal: At first, when officials charged Bi with imposture, he answered: "It was all Daogu who taught me.
translations.idiomatic: When officials first charged Bi with fraud, he replied, "Daogu taught me everything I did.

sentences.zh: 解衣即刑，卒無它異。

translations.literal: He removed his clothes and submitted to punishment, and in the end there was nothing else unusual.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped for execution, and in the end nothing else unusual occurred.

sentences.zh: 镈之貶，前坊州刺史班肅以嘗僚，獨餞於野，朝廷義之，擢為司封員外郎。

translations.literal: At Bo's demotion, the former prefect of Fangzhou, Ban Su, because they had once been colleagues, alone saw him off in the wilds; the court honored this and promoted him to outer-office member of the Directorate of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo was demoted, Ban Su, the former prefect of Fang Prefecture, alone saw him off in the countryside because they had once served together; the court admired his loyalty and promoted him to outer-office member of the Directorate of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 镈弟鏞，字龢卿，第進士。

translations.literal: Bo's younger brother Yong, styled Heqing, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's younger brother Yong, styled Heqing, earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 镈為相時，任河南少尹，見權寵太盛，每極言之，镈不悅，乃求分司為太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When Bo was chief minister, Yong served as vice-prefect of Henan; seeing that power and favor were too great, he spoke out against it to the utmost each time, Bo was displeased, and Yong therefore requested a detached-office post as Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: While Bo served as chief minister, Yong held the post of vice-prefect of Henan. Seeing that Bo's power and favor had grown excessive, he spoke out against it again and again until Bo grew displeased; Yong then requested a detached-office appointment as Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 镈敗，朝廷賢之，授國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Bo fell, the court regarded Yong as worthy and appointed him Rector of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After Bo's downfall, the court admired Yong's integrity and appointed him Rector of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 開成初，以太子少保卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era he died while serving as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaicheng era he died in office as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 鏞能屬文，工詩。

translations.literal: Yong could compose prose and was skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was an accomplished prose writer and a skilled poet.

sentences.zh: 為人寡言正色，衣冠甚偉，不屑世務，所交皆知名士。

translations.literal: As a man he spoke little and kept a stern countenance, his dress and bearing were very imposing, he disdained worldly affairs, and those he associated with were all famous scholars.
translations.idiomatic: A man of few words and stern bearing, he cut an imposing figure in dress and deportment, disdained worldly affairs, and kept company only with celebrated men of letters.

sentences.zh: 著書數十篇。

translations.literal: He authored several tens of essays.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote several dozen essays.

sentences.zh: 王播，字明敭，其先太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Bo, styled Mingyang, his ancestors were men of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo, styled Mingyang, came from a Taiyuan family.

sentences.zh: 父恕為揚州倉曹參軍，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father Shu served as grain-store aide of Yangzhou, and there the family settled.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu served as grain-store aide in Yang Prefecture, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 播，貞元中與弟炎、起皆有名，並擢進士，而播、起舉賢良方正異等。

translations.literal: Bo, in the Zhenyuan era, together with his younger brothers Yan and Qi all had fame; all passed the jinshi examination, and Bo and Qi were also raised in the exceptional grade of Worthy and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era Bo, together with his younger brothers Yan and Qi, all won renown; all three passed the jinshi examination, and Bo and Qi were also selected in the exceptional grade of the Worthy and Upright examination.

sentences.zh: 補盩厔尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi County.

sentences.zh: 以善治獄，御史中丞李汶薦為監察御史。

translations.literal: Because he was skilled at handling cases, the censor-in-chief Li Wen recommended him as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was skilled at handling legal cases, Censor-in-Chief Li Wen recommended him for appointment as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 雲陽丞源咸季坐賕免，賂有司復得調，播劾解其官。
