translations.literal: The assistant magistrate of Yunyang, Yuan Xianji, was removed from office for bribery, bribed the relevant offices and again obtained reassignment, and Bo impeached him and stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xianji, assistant magistrate of Yunyang, had been dismissed for bribery but bribed the relevant offices and secured a new appointment; Bo impeached him and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 歷侍御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 李實為京兆尹，與播遇諸衢。

translations.literal: Li Shi was Jingzhao intendant, and he met Bo in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi was serving as intendant of the capital district when he encountered Bo in the street.

sentences.zh: 故事，尹當避道揖，實不肯。

translations.literal: By precedent the intendant should yield the road and bow, but Shi would not.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the intendant was supposed to yield the road and bow, but Shi refused.

sentences.zh: 播移文詆之。

translations.literal: Bo sent a dispatch denouncing him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo sent an official dispatch denouncing him.

sentences.zh: 實大怒，表播為三原令，將折之，播受命，趨府謝如禮。

translations.literal: Shi was greatly angered, memorialized to appoint Bo magistrate of Sanyuan intending to break him, Bo accepted the order, and hurried to the office to pay thanks according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Shi flew into a rage and had Bo transferred to the post of magistrate of Sanyuan, intending to humiliate him; Bo accepted the appointment and promptly went to the intendant's office to pay his respects according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 邑中豪強犯法，未嘗輒貸，歲終課最。

translations.literal: When powerful men in the district violated the law, he never readily pardoned them, and at year's end his assessment ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: He never readily pardoned powerful local offenders, and at year's end his performance ranked first.

sentences.zh: 實重其才，更薦之，德宗將擢以要近，會母喪解。

translations.literal: Shi valued his talent and recommended him again; Dezong was about to promote him to an important nearby post when his mother's death obliged him to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Shi came to respect his ability and recommended him again; Emperor Dezong was about to promote him to an important post at court when the death of his mother forced him to leave office.

sentences.zh: 還，除駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: When he returned he was appointed outer-office member of the Directorate of Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to service he was appointed outer-office member of the Directorate of Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 長安令于頔奴客與民盜馬，吏系民而縱奴，播捕取，均其罰。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Chang'an, Yu Di's slave-guest and a commoner stole horses; officials detained the commoner but released the slave, and Bo seized and punished both, equalizing their penalties.
translations.idiomatic: A slave-guest of Yu Di, magistrate of Chang'an, and a commoner stole horses together; officials detained the commoner but let the slave go free, so Bo arrested both and imposed equal penalties.

sentences.zh: 遷工部郎中，知御史雜事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Ministry of Works and given charge of miscellaneous censorial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works and put in charge of miscellaneous censorial affairs.

sentences.zh: 刺舉不阿，有能稱。

translations.literal: In investigation and impeachment he did not bend, and he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In investigation and impeachment he never bent to favor, and he won a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 關中饑，諸鎮或閉糴，播以為言，三輔不乏。

translations.literal: Guanzhong suffered famine; some garrison commands closed grain sales, Bo spoke out against this, and the Three Adjuncts did not lack provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong suffered famine and some garrison commands hoarded grain by closing sales, Bo protested, and the Three Adjuncts did not go wanting.

sentences.zh: 歷虢州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李巽領鹽鐵，奏以副己。

translations.literal: Li Xun headed the salt and iron office and memorialized to have Bo serve as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, who headed the salt and iron office, memorialized to have Bo appointed as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 擢御史中丞，歲終，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor-in-chief, and at year's end was changed to Jingzhao intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief, and at the end of the year was made intendant of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 時禁屯列畿內者，出入屬佩劍，奸人冒之以剽劫，又勛將家馳獵近郊，播請一切苛止，盜賊不能隱，皆走出境。

translations.literal: At the time the forbidden garrisons stationed within the capital region went in and out with swords at their belts; evil men borrowed this to rob and plunder, and the families of meritorious generals also galloped to hunt in the near suburbs; Bo requested that all of this be strictly stopped, robbers could not hide, and all fled beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: At the time garrison troops stationed near the capital went about wearing swords on their belts, and criminals exploited this to rob and plunder; the families of meritorious generals also galloped out to hunt in the nearby suburbs. Bo requested that all such practices be strictly forbidden; thieves could no longer hide among them and fled beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以為能，進刑部侍郎，領諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Xianzong regarded him as capable, advanced him to vice-minister of justice, and had him head the salt and iron transport commissioner for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong judged him capable, promoted him to vice-minister of justice, and appointed him commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下多故，大理議讞，科條叢繁，播悉置格律坐隅，商處重輕，剖決如流，吏不能竄其私。

translations.literal: At that time the empire had many troubles; the Court of Judicial Review deliberated cases, and statutes were dense and numerous; Bo placed all regulations and statutes at his side, weighed severity and leniency, decided cases like flowing water, and clerks could not insert their private interests.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empire was beset by troubles, and the Court of Judicial Review was overwhelmed with cases under a dense thicket of statutes. Bo kept all regulations and statutes at hand, weighed each case's severity, and decided matters with fluent dispatch, leaving clerks no room to insert their private interests.

sentences.zh: 帝討淮西也，切於饋餉，播引程异自副，异尤通萬貨盈虛，使馳傳江淮，裒財用以給軍興，兵得無乏。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Huaixi, he was urgent about supplies; Bo brought in Cheng Yi as his deputy, Yi was especially versed in the surplus and deficit of all goods, had him travel by post-horse through the Jianghuai region, gathered wealth to supply the army's needs, and the troops did not suffer want.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Huaixi, supplies were urgently needed; Bo brought in Cheng Yi as his deputy. Yi was especially skilled at tracking the ebb and flow of goods and was sent racing by post-horse through the Jianghuai region to gather funds for the war effort, so that the army never went wanting.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，超拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his achievement and promoted him by special appointment to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his achievement and leapfrogged him to the post of Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 稍以資賄結宦要，中外以為言。

translations.literal: Gradually he used wealth and bribes to bind eunuch power-brokers, and inside and outside the court spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he used wealth and bribes to cultivate eunuch power-brokers, and criticism spread both inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 播薦皇甫鎛，及鎛用事，更忌播，而以异代使，播罷守本官。

translations.literal: Bo recommended Huangfu Bo; when Bo came to power he grew even more jealous of Wang Bo, and replaced Yi as commissioner, while Wang Bo was removed and kept only his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Bo had recommended Huangfu Bo; once Huangfu Bo came to power he grew jealous of Wang Bo, replaced Cheng Yi as commissioner, and had Wang Bo stripped of his commission while retaining only his original office.

sentences.zh: 久之，檢校戶部尚書，為劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made acting Minister of Revenue and military commissioner of Western Chuan in Southern Sword.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed acting Minister of Revenue and military commissioner of Western Chuan in Southern Sword.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，逐鎛，播求還。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended, Huangfu Bo was expelled, and Wang Bo requested to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong came to the throne, Huangfu Bo was driven out, and Wang Bo asked to return to court.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，召為刑部尚書，復領鹽鐵，進中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing era he was summoned as Minister of Justice, again headed salt and iron, and advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changqing era he was recalled as Minister of Justice, again put in charge of salt and iron, and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat with the title of Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 時權幸競進，播賴其力至宰相，專務將迎，居位無所裨益，復失河北，眾望不厭，乃以檢校尚書右僕射出為淮南節度使，仍領使職，不肯易印，詔聽自隨。

translations.literal: At the time the favored and powerful competed to advance; Bo relied on their strength to reach the chief ministership, devoted himself solely to courting favor, in office contributed nothing of benefit, Hebei was again lost, public expectation was not satisfied, and so he was sent out as acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and military commissioner of Huainan, still retaining the commissioner's office, refusing to surrender the seal, and an edict allowed him to keep it with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the favored and powerful were all scrambling for advancement; Bo had relied on their support to reach the chief ministership, devoting himself solely to courting favor and contributing nothing of substance in office. When Hebei was lost again and public confidence collapsed, he was sent out as acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and military commissioner of Huainan, while still retaining his commissioner's seal—he refused to surrender it, and an edict allowed him to keep it.

sentences.zh: 是時，南方旱歉，人相食，播掊斂不少衰，民皆怨之。

translations.literal: At that time the south suffered drought and crop failure, people ate one another, Bo's exactions did not diminish in the least, and the people all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the south suffered drought and famine until people were eating one another, yet Bo's exactions did not slacken in the least, and the people resented him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 然浚七里港以便漕引，後賴其利。

translations.literal: Yet he dredged the Qili Harbor to facilitate canal transport, and later they relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he dredged Qili Harbor to improve the canal route, and later generations benefited from the work.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，就進檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended, he was immediately advanced to acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong came to the throne, Bo was immediately promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，入朝，拜左僕射，復輔政，累封太原郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he entered court, was appointed Left Vice Director, again assisted in government, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 827 he came to court, was appointed Left Vice Director, again joined the governing council, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時韋處厚當國，以獻替自任，天子向之。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Chuhou held the state, took upon himself the duty of offering and replacing policy, and the Son of Heaven turned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Chuhou directed state affairs, taking upon himself the duty of advising and correcting policy, and the emperor looked to him.

sentences.zh: 播專以錢谷進，不甚與事。

translations.literal: Bo relied solely on money and grain contributions to advance and did not much take part in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bo relied chiefly on financial contributions to maintain his standing and took little part in governing.

sentences.zh: 居位四年，卒，年七十二，贈太尉，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He held office four years, died at age seventy-two, was posthumously granted Grand Marshal, and was given the posthumous title Respected.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for four years, then died at seventy-two; he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Marshal and given the posthumous name Respected.

sentences.zh: 播少孤貧，自刻苦，至成立，居官以強濟稱。

translations.literal: Bo was orphaned and poor in youth, applied himself to hardship from the start, until he established himself, and in office was known for forceful effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was orphaned and poor in youth and drove himself through hardship until he made his way in the world; in office he was known for forceful effectiveness.

sentences.zh: 天性勤吏職，每視簿領紛積於前，人所不堪者，播反用為樂。

translations.literal: By nature he was diligent in clerical duties; whenever he saw ledgers piled in confusion before him, what others could not endure, Bo instead took as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was devoted to administrative work; where others would have been overwhelmed by ledgers piled high before them, Bo took pleasure in the task.

sentences.zh: 所署吏，茍無大罪，以歲勞增秩而已，卒不易所職。

translations.literal: Among the clerks he appointed, if there was no great crime, he merely increased rank for yearly service and in the end never changed their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Among the clerks he appointed, if they had committed no serious offense he merely raised their rank for years of service and almost never changed their assignments.

sentences.zh: 雅善占奏，雖數十事，未嘗書於笏。

translations.literal: He was by nature skilled at extemporaneous memorials; even for several tens of matters he never wrote on his tablet.
translations.idiomatic: He was naturally skilled at extemporaneous memorials; even when reporting on dozens of matters he never needed to write notes on his court tablet.

sentences.zh: 再領鹽鐵，嗜權利，不復初操。

translations.literal: When he again headed salt and iron, he became addicted to power and profit and no longer kept his original conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When he again took charge of salt and iron, he grew addicted to power and profit and abandoned his earlier standards.

sentences.zh: 重賦取，以正額月進為羨余，歲百萬緡。

translations.literal: He imposed heavy levies and presented the regular quota's monthly tribute as surplus, one million strings per year.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed heavy levies and presented the regular quota's monthly tribute as surplus revenue, amounting to one million strings of cash each year.

sentences.zh: 自淮南還，獻玉帶十有三、銀碗數千、綾四十萬，遂再得相雲。

translations.literal: Returning from Huainan, he presented thirteen jade belts, several thousand silver bowls, and four hundred thousand bolts of silk, and thus again obtained the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from Huainan he presented thirteen jade belts, several thousand silver bowls, and four hundred thousand bolts of silk, and thereby regained the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 起，字舉之，釋褐校書郎，補藍田尉。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Juzhi, upon leaving the hempen robe was appointed collator, and was appointed magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, styled Juzhi, upon entering official service was appointed collator and then magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫辟為淮南掌書記，以殿中侍御史入兼集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: Li Jifu recruited him as chief secretary of Huainan; he entered as palace attendant censor and concurrently served as resident academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu recruited him as chief secretary in Huainan; he entered court as palace attendant censor and concurrently served as resident academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 元和末，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era he was promoted in succession to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Yuanhe era he had risen to the post of Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 數上疏諫穆宗畋遊事，歲中考第一。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials remonstrating against Muzong's hunting and pleasure outings, and in the yearly assessment ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials remonstrating against Muzong's hunting and pleasure outings, and ranked first in the yearly performance assessment.

sentences.zh: 錢徽坐貢舉失實貶，詔起覆核，起建言：「以所試送宰相閱可否，然後付有司。」

translations.literal: Qian Hui was demoted for falsehood in the tribute selection examination; an edict ordered Qi to review it, and Qi proposed: "Send the examination papers to the chief ministers to approve or reject, and only afterward hand them to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hui was demoted for irregularities in the civil service examination; an edict ordered Qi to review the case, and Qi proposed, "The examination papers should be sent to the chief ministers for approval or rejection before being handed to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 議者謂起為失職。

translations.literal: Commentators said Qi had failed in his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Qi had failed in his duty.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 李叛，與播俱上疏請詔王智興討之，卒定其亂。

translations.literal: Li rebelled; together with Bo he submitted a memorial requesting an edict for Wang Zhixing to suppress him, and in the end the rebellion was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Li rebelled, Qi and Bo jointly submitted a memorial asking that Wang Zhixing be ordered to suppress him, and the rebellion was eventually put down.

sentences.zh: 賜金紫，拜河南尹，進吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was granted gold seal and purple robe, appointed intendant of Henan, and advanced to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the gold seal and purple robe, appointed intendant of Henan, and promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 方播以僕射居相，避選曹，改兵部，為集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: Just as Bo served as chief minister while holding the vice directorship, Qi avoided the selection bureau, changed to the Ministry of War, and became an academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: While Bo was serving as chief minister from the vice directorship, Qi stepped aside from the selection bureau, transferred to the Ministry of War, and became an academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 拜陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the Shan-Guo circuit.

sentences.zh: 時亳州刺史李繁以擅誅賊抵罪，起言：「繁父有功，而二千石不宜償賊死。」

translations.literal: At the time the prefect of Bozhou, Li Fan, was charged with executing bandits on his own authority; Qi said: "Fan's father had merit, and a two-thousand-dan official should not pay with his life for bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Fan, prefect of Bo Prefecture, was charged with executing bandits on his own authority; Qi argued, "Fan's father had rendered meritorious service, and a prefect should not pay with his life for killing bandits.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 入拜尚書左丞，以戶部尚書判度支。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, and as Minister of Revenue he adjudicated the revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court and was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, serving concurrently as Minister of Revenue with charge of the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 靈武、邠、寧多曠土，奏為營田，以省饋免。

translations.literal: In Lingwu, Bin, and Ning there was much idle land; he memorialized to establish garrison farms in order to reduce supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Lingwu, Bin, and Ning there was much unused land; he memorialized to establish garrison farms in order to reduce the cost of supply transport.

sentences.zh: 歷河中節度使。

translations.literal: He served successively as military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 方蝗旱，粟價騰踴，起下令家得儲三十斛，斥其餘以市，否者死。

translations.literal: Just then there were locusts and drought, grain prices soared, Qi ordered that each household might store thirty hu and must sell the rest on the market, on pain of death.
translations.idiomatic: Just then locusts and drought drove grain prices skyward; Qi ordered that each household might keep thirty hu in store and must sell the rest on the market, on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 神策士怙勢不從，寘於法。

translations.literal: Shence soldiers relied on their power and would not obey; he placed them under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Shence soldiers relied on their influence and refused to comply; he punished them according to the law.

sentences.zh: 由是廥積咸出，民賴以生。

translations.literal: Because of this stored grain all came out, and the people relied on it to live.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, hoarded grain poured onto the market and the people were saved from starvation.

sentences.zh: 召授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 以檢校尚書右僕射為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: As acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs he served as military commissioner of Southeastern Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and military commissioner of Southeastern Shannan.

sentences.zh: 濱漢塘堰聯屬，吏弗完治，起至部，先修復，與民約為水令，遂無凶年。

translations.literal: Along the Han River dikes and weirs were linked in succession; officials did not complete their repair; when Qi reached his post he first restored them, made water regulations with the people, and thereafter there were no disastrous years.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Han River dikes and weirs stretched in succession, but officials had left them unrepaired; when Qi arrived he restored them first, established water regulations with the people, and thereafter the region suffered no disastrous floods.

sentences.zh: 李訓為宰相，起門生也，欲引與共政，即加銀青光祿大夫，復以兵部尚書召判戶部。

translations.literal: Li Xun was chief minister; Qi was his student and he wished to bring him in to govern together, immediately added the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and again summoned him as Minister of War to adjudicate the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun became chief minister; Qi had been his student, and Xun wished to bring him into the government, immediately granting him the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and recalling him as Minister of War with concurrent charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 訓敗，起素長厚，人不以訓諉之，止罷其判。

translations.literal: When Xun fell, Qi had long been generous and steady, people did not impute Xun's fault to him, and only his concurrent adjudication was removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun fell, Qi had long been known for his generosity and steadiness, and no one blamed him for Xun's crimes; he was merely stripped of his concurrent charge.

sentences.zh: 俄加皇太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon he was added as Reader to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Reader to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 文宗上文，好古學，是時，鄭覃以經術進，起以敦博顯，帝數訪逮時政。

translations.literal: Wenzong had ascended and loved ancient learning; at this time Zheng Tan advanced through classical learning, Qi was distinguished for solid breadth, and the emperor repeatedly consulted him on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had come to the throne with a love of classical learning; at this time Zheng Tan had risen through mastery of the classics, while Qi was renowned for solid erudition, and the emperor repeatedly consulted him on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 因積雨，願寬逐臣過惡，又短鮑叔終身不忘人過，以解帝錮人意。

translations.literal: Because of prolonged rain, he asked to relax the past faults of exiled officials, and also briefly cited Bao Shu, who throughout his life never forgot others' faults, in order to loosen the emperor's habit of confining men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the prolonged rains, he asked that punishments on exiled officials be eased, and also invoked Bao Shu, who never forgot others' faults throughout his life, in order to soften the emperor's habit of holding men's transgressions against them.

sentences.zh: 俄兼太常卿、禮儀使。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commissioner of Ritual Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commissioner of Ritual Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝題詩太子笏以賜，詔畫像便殿，號「當世仲尼」，其寵遇如此。

translations.literal: The emperor inscribed a poem on the crown prince's tablet and bestowed it, ordered his portrait painted in the side hall, and titled him "the Confucius of the age"—such was his favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inscribed a poem on the crown prince's court tablet and bestowed it on him, ordered his portrait painted in the side hall, and styled him "the Confucius of the age"—such was the favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 又使廣《五位圖》，俾太子知古今治亂。

translations.literal: He also had the Expanded 《Chart of the Five Positions》 enlarged, so the heir might know governance and disorder through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the Expanded 《Chart of the Five Positions》 enlarged so the heir might learn governance and disorder through the ages.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，入翰林，為侍講學士，改太子少師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng he entered the Hanlin Academy as a lecturing academician and was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 838 he entered the Hanlin Academy as a lecturing academician and was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 起治生無檢，所得祿賜為僮婢盜有，貧不能自存。

translations.literal: In managing his livelihood Qi was without restraint; what he received in salary and gifts was stolen by servants and slaves, and he was too poor to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: In managing his livelihood Qi was without restraint; salary and gifts were stolen by servants and slaves until he could scarcely support himself.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，詔月益仙韶院錢三十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this and ordered that thirty thousand cash from the Xianshao Court be added to his monthly stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew this and ordered that thirty thousand cash from the Xianshao Court be added to his monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 議者謂與玩臣分給，可恥也。

translations.literal: Commentators said this was shared with favored performers and was shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said this was shared with favored performers and was shameful.

sentences.zh: 起賴其入，不克讓。

translations.literal: Qi relied on the income and could not decline it.
translations.idiomatic: Qi relied on the income and could not bring himself to decline it.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，為章陵鹵簿使、東都留守。

translations.literal: When Wuzong succeeded, he was made director of funeral honors for Zhangling and eastern capital intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong succeeded, he was made director of funeral honors for Zhangling and eastern capital intendant.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部尚書，判太常卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Personnel and concurrently Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of Personnel and concurrently Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 帝患選士不得才，特命起典貢舉。

translations.literal: The emperor worried that selected scholars lacked talent and specially ordered Qi to preside over the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried that selected scholars lacked talent and specially ordered Qi to preside over the examinations.

sentences.zh: 進尚書左僕射，封魏郡公。

translations.literal: He advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 凡四舉士，皆知名者，人伏其鑒。

translations.literal: In all four examinations the men he raised were famous; people submitted to his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In all four examinations the men he raised were famous; people submitted to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 擢山南西道節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military commissioner of Southern Sword in the west and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military commissioner of Southern Sword in the west and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 以夙儒兼宰相秩，前世所罕。

translations.literal: To be a longtime Confucian and also hold chief minister rank was rare in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: To be a longtime Confucian and also hold chief minister rank was rare in former ages.

sentences.zh: 入辭，帝勞曰：「宰相無內外。

translations.literal: On entering to take leave the emperor comforted him, saying: "A chief minister has no inner or outer.
translations.idiomatic: On entering to take leave the emperor comforted him, saying, "A chief minister has no inner or outer.

sentences.zh: 公，國耆老，朕有闕，當以聞。」

translations.literal: You are the state's elder; if We have failings, you should report them.
translations.idiomatic: You are the state's elder; if We have failings, you should report them.

sentences.zh: 宴賜備厚。

translations.literal: The feast and gifts were fully generous.
translations.idiomatic: The feast and gifts were fully generous.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，檢校司空，以疾願代，不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzong's reign he was made acting Minister of Works; because of illness he asked to be replaced, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xuanzong's reign he was made acting Minister of Works; because of illness he asked to be replaced, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十八，贈太尉，謚曰文懿。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-eight; was posthumously made Grand Marshal and given the posthumous name "Cultured and Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-eight and was posthumously made Grand Marshal with the posthumous name "Cultured and Excellent."

sentences.zh: 喪還，命使者吊其家，葬及祥亦如之。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession returned, the emperor ordered envoys to condole at his house; burial and the second mourning rite were likewise honored.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession returned, the emperor ordered envoys to condole at his house; burial and the second mourning rite were likewise honored.

sentences.zh: 起性友悌，播喪，哀戚加於人。

translations.literal: Qi was by nature friendly and fraternal; when Bo died his grief exceeded that of others.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was by nature friendly and fraternal; when Bo died his grief exceeded that of others.

sentences.zh: 嗜學，非寢食不輒廢。

translations.literal: He loved learning and would not set it aside except for sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and would not set it aside except for sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 天下之書無不讀，一經目，弗忘也。

translations.literal: There was no book under Heaven he did not read; once he passed his eyes over a classic he did not forget it.
translations.idiomatic: There was no book under Heaven he did not read; once he passed his eyes over a text he did not forget it.

sentences.zh: 莊恪太子薨，詔為哀冊，詞情淒惋，當世稱之。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent Zhuangke died, an edict ordered him to compose the lament; the words were mournful and touching, and men of the time praised them.
translations.idiomatic: When Heir Apparent Zhuangke died, an edict ordered him to compose the lament; the words were mournful and touching, and men of the time praised them.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以疑事令使者口質，起具榜子附使者上，凡成十篇，號曰《寫宣》。

translations.literal: The emperor once had envoys orally examine him on doubtful matters; Qi prepared placards for the envoys to carry up, ten pieces in all, titled 《Writings for Imperial Inquiry》.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once had envoys orally examine him on doubtful matters; Qi prepared placards for the envoys to carry up, ten pieces in all, titled 《Writings for Imperial Inquiry》.

sentences.zh: 它撰集亦多。

translations.literal: His other collected writings were also many.
translations.idiomatic: His other collected writings were also many.

sentences.zh: 炎終太常博士。

translations.literal: Yan ended as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ended as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 子鐸、鐐自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons Duo and Liao have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Duo and Liao have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 起子龜、式。

translations.literal: Qi's sons Gui and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's sons Gui and Shi.

sentences.zh: 龜，字大年，性高簡，博知書傳，無貴胄氣。

translations.literal: Gui, styled Danian, was by nature lofty and spare, broadly knowing books and records, without the air of noble kin.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, styled Danian, was by nature lofty and spare, broadly knowing books and records, without the air of noble kin.

sentences.zh: 常以光福第賓客多，更住永達裏，林木窮僻，構半隱亭以自適。

translations.literal: He often said the Guangfu residence had too many guests and moved to Yongda Lane, where trees and woods were remote; he built a half-recluse pavilion for his own ease.
translations.idiomatic: He often said the Guangfu residence had too many guests and moved to Yongda Lane, where trees and woods were remote; he built a half-recluse pavilion for his own ease.

sentences.zh: 侍父至河中，廬中條山，朔望一歸省，州人號「郎君谷」，未始以人事自嬰。

translations.literal: Attending his father to Hezhong, he lodged on Mount Tiao in the mourning hut; on the first and fifteenth of each month he returned once to visit—the people of the prefecture called it "the Gentleman's Valley"—and he never troubled himself with worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Attending his father to Hezhong, he lodged on Mount Tiao in the mourning hut; on the first and fifteenth of each month he returned once to visit—the people of the prefecture called it "the Gentleman's Valley"—and he never troubled himself with worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 武宗雅知之，以左拾遺召。

translations.literal: Wuzong knew him well by reputation and summoned him as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong knew him well by reputation and summoned him as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 入謝，自陳病不任職，詔許。

translations.literal: On entering to give thanks he himself stated that illness made him unfit for office; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: On entering to give thanks he himself stated that illness made him unfit for office; an edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 終父喪，召為右補闕。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning ended he was summoned as Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's mourning ended he was summoned as Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 再擢屯田員外郎，稱疾去。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to outer-office member of the Board of Agriculture and, citing illness, left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to outer-office member of the Board of Agriculture and, citing illness, left office.

sentences.zh: 崔玙觀察宣歙，表為副，龜樂宛陵山水，故從之。

translations.literal: Cui Yu was military commissioner of Xuan and She and memorialized him as deputy; Gui delighted in the landscape of Wanling and therefore followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yu was military commissioner of Xuan and She and memorialized him as deputy; Gui delighted in the landscape of Wanling and therefore followed him.

sentences.zh: 入為祠部郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He entered service as director of the Board of Sacrifices and reviser of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as director of the Board of Sacrifices and reviser of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，知制誥。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era he drafted imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era he drafted imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 鐸為相，改太常少卿、同州刺史。

translations.literal: When Duo became chief minister he was changed to Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo became chief minister he was changed to Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 牙將白約素暴橫，嘗嘩言月稟薄，以動士心為亂，龜捕殺之，人皆震栗。

translations.literal: The military adjutant Bai Yue had long been violent and overbearing; he once clamored that monthly rations were thin to stir soldiers' hearts toward rebellion; Gui arrested and killed him, and all were shaken in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The military adjutant Bai Yue had long been violent and overbearing; he once clamored that monthly rations were thin to stir soldiers' hearts toward rebellion; Gui arrested and killed him, and all were shaken in fear.

sentences.zh: 徙浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 初，式臨州有惠政，人聞其至，歡迎之。

translations.literal: At first, when Shi governed the prefecture he had benevolent administration; when people heard Gui was coming they welcomed him joyfully.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Shi governed the prefecture he had benevolent administration; when people heard Gui was coming they welcomed him joyfully.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子蕘，力學，有文辭，以鐸當國，不貢進士。

translations.literal: His son Rao studied hard and had literary talent; because Duo was in power he did not present himself for the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rao studied hard and had literary talent; because Duo was in power he did not present himself for the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 終右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He ended as outer-office member of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as outer-office member of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 式以蔭為太子正字，擢賢良方正科，累遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Shi entered office by hereditary privilege as rectifier to the heir, was selected in the erudite examination in upright conduct, and was promoted in succession to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi entered office by hereditary privilege as rectifier to the heir, was selected in the erudite examination in upright conduct, and was promoted in succession to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 少節儉，巧於宦，因鄭註以交王守澄，中丞歸融劾之，出為江陵少尹。

translations.literal: In youth he was frugal and clever at court maneuvering; through Zheng Zhu he joined Wang Shoucheng; Censor-in-Chief Gui Rong impeached him and he was sent out as vice-prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was frugal and clever at court maneuvering; through Zheng Zhu he joined Wang Shoucheng; Censor-in-Chief Gui Rong impeached him and he was sent out as vice-prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 大中中，為晉州刺史，飾郵傳，器用畢給。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he was prefect of Jin Prefecture; he adorned relay posts and furnished all utensils completely.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era he was prefect of Jin Prefecture; he adorned relay posts and furnished all utensils completely.

sentences.zh: 會河曲大歉，民流徙，佗州不納，獨式勞恤之，活數千人。

translations.literal: When the bend of the Yellow River suffered great famine the people fled; other prefectures would not receive them, but Shi alone labored to comfort them and kept several thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the bend of the Yellow River suffered great famine the people fled; other prefectures would not receive them, but Shi alone labored to comfort them and kept several thousand alive.

sentences.zh: 時特峨胡亦饑，將入寇汾、澮，聞式嚴備，不敢道境，報其種落曰：「晉州刺史當避之！」

translations.literal: At the time the Te'e Hu were also famine-struck and wished to invade Fen and Huai; hearing that Shi was strictly prepared they dared not cross the border and reported to their tribes: "The Jin Prefecture intendant should be avoided!
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Te'e Hu were also famine-struck and wished to invade Fen and Huai; hearing that Shi was strictly prepared they dared not cross the border and reported to their tribes, "The Jin Prefecture intendant should be avoided!

sentences.zh: 以善最稱。

translations.literal: He was praised for the finest administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was praised for the finest administration.

sentences.zh: 徙安南都護。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Protector-General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Protector-General of Annan.

sentences.zh: 故都護田早作木柵，歲率緡錢，既不時完，而所責益急。

translations.literal: The former protector Tian Zao built wooden palisades and every year exacted strings in cash; they were not finished on time yet what was demanded grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The former protector Tian Zao built wooden palisades and every year exacted strings in cash; they were not finished on time yet what was demanded grew more urgent.

sentences.zh: 式取一年賦市芍木，豎周十二里，罷歲賦外率以紓齊人。

translations.literal: Shi took one year's levy to buy peony wood, set it in a ring twelve li around, and abolished the extra annual exactions to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shi took one year's levy to buy peony wood, set it in a ring twelve li around, and abolished the extra annual exactions to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 浚壕繚柵，外植刺竹，寇不可冒。

translations.literal: He dredged moats and linked palisades, planted thorn bamboo outside, and raiders could not break through.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged moats and linked palisades, planted thorn bamboo outside, and raiders could not break through.

sentences.zh: 後蠻兵入掠錦田步，式使譯者開諭，一昔去，謝曰：「我自縛叛獠，非為寇也。」

translations.literal: Later southern tribes entered to plunder Jintian Step; Shi had interpreters open persuasion and in one night they withdrew, apologizing: "We ourselves bound rebellious tribesmen—it was not to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Later southern tribes entered to plunder Jintian Step; Shi had interpreters open persuasion and in one night they withdrew, apologizing, "We ourselves bound rebellious tribesmen—it was not to raid.

sentences.zh: 忠武戍卒服短後褐，以黃冒首，南方號「黃頭軍」，天下銳卒也。

translations.literal: The loyal-wu garrison soldiers wore short jackets with yellow cloth over the head; the south called them "Yellow-Head Army"—the empire's sharpest troops.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal-wu garrison soldiers wore short jackets with yellow cloth over the head; the south called them "Yellow-Head Army"—the empire's sharpest troops.

sentences.zh: 初，交阯數有變，懼式威，不自安，嘩曰：「黃頭軍將度海襲我矣！」

translations.literal: At first Jiaozhi had many disturbances and feared Shi's might, could not rest easy, and clamored: "The Yellow-Head Army is about to cross the sea and attack us!
translations.idiomatic: At first Jiaozhi had many disturbances and feared Shi's might, could not rest easy, and clamored, "The Yellow-Head Army is about to cross the sea and attack us!

sentences.zh: 相率夜圍城，合噪：「請都護北歸，我當抗黃頭軍。」

translations.literal: They joined by night to surround the city, shouting together: "Let the protector return north; we will resist the Yellow-Head Army."
translations.idiomatic: They joined by night to surround the city, shouting together, "Let the protector return north; we will resist the Yellow-Head Army."

sentences.zh: 式徐被甲，引家僮乘城責讓，矢旝交發，叛者走。

translations.literal: Shi slowly donned armor, led household retainers onto the wall to rebuke them; arrows and banners flew back and forth and the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shi slowly donned armor, led household retainers onto the wall to rebuke them; arrows and banners flew back and forth and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 翌日，盡捕斬之。

translations.literal: The next day he captured and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he captured and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 初，容管災歉，不歲貢，式始上輸，大犒宴軍中。

translations.literal: At first Rongguan suffered disaster and famine and did not submit annual tribute for years; Shi was the first to send tribute upstream and greatly feasted the army.
translations.idiomatic: At first Rongguan suffered disaster and famine and did not submit annual tribute for years; Shi was the first to send tribute upstream and greatly feasted the army.

sentences.zh: 歸質外蕃，而占城、真臘慕義，悉入獻，亦還所掠王民。

translations.literal: Returning he presented foreign tribes; Champa and Zhenla admired righteousness and all came to offer tribute, also returning captured royal subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Returning he presented foreign tribes; Champa and Zhenla admired righteousness and all came to offer tribute, also returning captured royal subjects.

sentences.zh: 寧國劇賊仇甫亂，明越觀察使鄭祗德不能討，宰相選式往代，詔可，因至京師。

translations.literal: In Ningguo the fierce bandit Qiu Fu rebelled; Ming-Yue military commissioner Zheng Zhide could not suppress him; the chief minister chose Shi to replace him; an edict approved, and he therefore came to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Ningguo the fierce bandit Qiu Fu rebelled; Ming-Yue Military Commissioner Zheng Zhide could not suppress him; the chief minister chose Shi to replace him; an edict approved, and he therefore came to the capital.

sentences.zh: 懿宗問方略，對曰：「第假臣兵，寇不足平也。」

translations.literal: Yizong asked his strategy; he answered: "Only lend your servant troops and the bandits are not enough to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong asked his strategy; he answered, "Only lend your servant troops and the bandits are not enough to pacify.

sentences.zh: 左右宦要皆曰：「兵眾則饋多，當惜天下費。」

translations.literal: Nearby eunuch favorites all said: "Many troops mean much supply—one should spare the empire's expense."
translations.idiomatic: Nearby eunuch favorites all said, "Many troops mean much supply—one should spare the empire's expense."

sentences.zh: 式奏：「盜若猖狂，天誅不亟決，東南征賦闕矣，寧得以億萬計之乎？

translations.literal: Shi memorialized: "If the robbers run wild and Heaven's punishment is not swiftly decided, the southeast's levies will be lost—can one reckon it in tens of millions?
translations.idiomatic: Shi memorialized, "If the robbers run wild and Heaven's punishment is not swiftly decided, the southeast's levies will be lost—can one reckon it in tens of millions?

sentences.zh: 兵多則功速費寡。

translations.literal: Many troops mean quick achievement and little expense.
translations.idiomatic: Many troops mean quick achievement and little expense.

sentences.zh: 二者孰利？」

translations.literal: Which of the two is advantageous?
translations.idiomatic: Which of the two is advantageous?

sentences.zh: 帝顧左右曰：「宜與兵。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to those nearby and said: "He should be given troops."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to those nearby and said, "He should be given troops."

sentences.zh: 於是詔益許、滑、淮南兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict added troops from Xu, Hua, and Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict added troops from Xu, Hua, and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 式發自光福裏第，麾幟皆東靡，獵獵有聲，喜曰：「是謂得天時矣！」

translations.literal: When Shi set out from his Guangfu Lane residence the banners all leaned eastward, rustling with sound; he said in delight: "This is called obtaining Heaven's season!
translations.idiomatic: When Shi set out from his Guangfu Lane residence the banners all leaned eastward, rustling with sound; he said in delight, "This is called obtaining Heaven's season!

sentences.zh: 聞賊用騎兵，乃閱所部，得吐蕃、回鶻遷隸數百，發龍陂監牧馬起用之，集土團諸兒為向導，擒甫斬之。

translations.literal: Hearing the bandits used cavalry, he reviewed his command and found several hundred relocated Tibetans and Uyghurs; he issued horses from Longpo stud farms to mount them, gathered local militia youths as guides, and captured Fu and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the bandits used cavalry, he reviewed his command and found several hundred relocated Tibetans and Uyghurs; he issued horses from Longpo stud farms to mount them, gathered local militia youths as guides, and captured Fu and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 加檢校右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was additionally made acting Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made acting Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 餘姚民徐澤專魚鹽之利，慈溪民陳瑊冒名仕至縣令，皆豪縱，州不能制。

translations.literal: The Yuyao man Xu Ze monopolized profit from fish and salt; the Cixi man Chen Zhen falsely took office name to reach magistrate—both were overbearing and violent and the prefecture could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuyao man Xu Ze monopolized profit from fish and salt; the Cixi man Chen Zhen falsely took office name to reach magistrate—both were overbearing and violent and the prefecture could not control them.

sentences.zh: 式曰：「甫竊發，不足畏；

translations.literal: Shi said: "Fu's sudden rising is not worth fear;
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "Fu's sudden rising is not worth fear;

sentences.zh: 若澤、瑊，乃巨猾也。」

translations.literal: but Ze and Zhen are great scoundrels.
translations.idiomatic: but Ze and Zhen are great scoundrels.

sentences.zh: 窮治其奸，皆榜死。

translations.literal: He thoroughly investigated their crimes and both were flogged to death.
translations.idiomatic: He thoroughly investigated their crimes and both were flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 咸通三年，徐州銀刀軍亂，以式檢校工部尚書，徙武寧節度使，詔許、滑兵自隨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiantong the Silver Blade Army of Xuzhou rebelled; Shi was made acting Minister of Works and transferred to military commissioner of Wu-Ning; an edict allowed Xu and Hua troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiantong the Silver Blade Army of Xuzhou rebelled; Shi was made acting Minister of Works and transferred to military commissioner of Wu-Ning; an edict allowed Xu and Hua troops to follow him.

sentences.zh: 視事三日，悉以計誅亂兵。

translations.literal: Three days after assuming office he used stratagems to execute all the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after assuming office he used stratagems to execute all the mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 會詔降武寧為團練，罷歸。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict reduced Wu-Ning to a training circuit and he was dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that an edict reduced Wu-Ning to a training circuit and he was dismissed and returned.

sentences.zh: 終左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: He ended as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：裴延齡引經誼惑其主，以不忠為忠。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Pei Yanling cited canonical principle to delude his lord, making disloyalty appear loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Pei Yanling cited canonical principle to delude his lord, making disloyalty appear as loyalty.

sentences.zh: 德宗倚延齡、韋渠牟等商天下成敗，自謂明而卒陷不明。

translations.literal: Dezong relied on Yanling, Wei Qumou, and others to bargain over whether the empire would succeed or fail, believing himself enlightened yet in the end falling into unenlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong relied on Yanling, Wei Qumou, and others to bargain over whether the empire would succeed or fail, believing himself enlightened yet in the end falling into unenlightenment.

sentences.zh: 君臣回沈，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Sovereign and ministers sank together—should this not warn us!
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign and ministers sank together—should this not warn us!

sentences.zh: 憲宗銳於立功，而皇甫镈以聚斂取宰相。

translations.literal: Xianzong was sharp in establishing merit, yet Huangfu Bo took the chief ministership through gathering wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was sharp in establishing merit, yet Huangfu Bo took the chief ministership through gathering wealth.

sentences.zh: 夫宰相者，乃天下選，彼暫勞一功，烏足勝任哉？

translations.literal: A chief minister is the empire's choice; a man who for a moment toils at one achievement—how can he be adequate to the post?
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister is the empire's choice; a man who for a moment toils at one achievement—how can he be adequate to the post?

sentences.zh: 中興之不終，有為而然。

translations.literal: That the restoration did not reach completion had its causes in what men did.
translations.idiomatic: That the restoration did not reach completion had its causes in what men did.
